### Dragon Rider Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/dragon-rider-duo

A viking rider and a cardboard dragon, ready to fly over the neighborhood.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 30 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 brown t-shirt and 1 pair dark pants for the rider (make: from closet)
- Gray felt, 2 yards, or 1 old gray blanket for the dragon tunic (buy: craft store or thrift store)
- 1 large cardboard box for wings and tail (make: collect spares)
- Black and yellow craft foam, 1 sheet each for the dragon eyes (buy: craft store)
- 1 faux-fur vest or brown scarf for the rider (make: from closet)
- 1 headband for the dragon eyes
- Scissors, tape, and string, 6 feet (make: household tools)

Steps:
1. Draw the wing shape on paper first and hold it against the dragon person's back: wings should reach from shoulder to hip.
2. Cut two wing shapes and a long tail from the cardboard box with the scissors.
3. Cut the wings smaller than the paper test, not bigger: oversized cardboard wings hit every doorway. Tape all cut edges smooth before wearing.
4. Glue the black and yellow foam eyes to a headband for the dragon head. The rider wears the faux-fur vest over the brown t-shirt.
5. Safety: Keep wing tips above waist height and tape all cardboard edges smooth so nobody gets scratched.
6. Rider stands in front with arms out like steering; dragon crouches behind with wings spread. Take the flying photo.
7. Optional pro finish: tape a row of small cardboard triangles along the dragon's shoulders as back ridges. Ridges plus wings read as dragon; wings alone read as bird.

Q: How do you keep cardboard wings up?
A: Tape them to the gray felt tunic, not the person, with wide packing-tape tabs on both sides. Taped wings stay up for hours; glued wings peel.

Q: What is the best pose for the photo?
A: Rider stands in front with arms out like steering, dragon crouches behind with wings spread. The crouch sells the size difference.

### Emerald Witch

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emerald-witch

An all-green-everything gown, dramatic makeup, and a pointy hat gone couture.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 long green dress, or green fabric, 3 yards (buy: fabric store)
- 1 sheet black cardboard, 22x28 inches, for the hat (buy: craft store; a box painted black works too)
- Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- Black eyeliner, 1, and dark green eye shadow, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Hot glue gun with glue sticks, 1 set and scissors, 1 pair
- 1 broom from home for a prop (make: use what you own)

Steps:
1. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue, since the nozzle and glue get very hot.
2. Sew or hot glue the green fabric into a long gown, leaving the hem ragged.
3. Measure the head first, then roll the black cardboard into a tall cone and tape it loosely to check the fit before gluing.
4. Glue a wide cardboard brim to its base with the hot glue. Hot glue sets fast and cannot be repositioned, so test the cone shape dry first.
5. Paint the face green with the green face paint. Draw on the black eyeliner and the dark green eye shadow.
6. Carry the broom bristle-up so it does not trip anyone.
7. Optional pro finish: fray the gown hem by cutting 2-inch slits every few inches. A ragged hem is the difference between green dress and witch's gown.

Q: How do you get green face paint off?
A: Wash with a gentle cleanser and soap, not just water: green needs soap. Moisturize after, and patch-test on the jawline first if skin is sensitive.

Q: What if I cannot sew the gown?
A: Hot glue works: fold the fabric around the body and glue the seam. It holds for one night and nobody sees the seam from the front.

### Emoji Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emoji-crew

Everyone picks an emoji: a yellow tee plus a big printed face.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 yellow t-shirt per person (buy: craft store, or use one you own)
- 1 large white paper plate, 10-inch, or cardboard circle per person (make: use what you own)
- Markers in black, red, and blue, 1 set (make: use what you own)
- Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Buy yellow t-shirts if the crew does not own them.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the paper plates or cardboard circles.
3. Draw the emoji on the paper plate first in pencil, then go over it with the markers.
4. Trim the plate or cardboard circle only where it overhangs the design. Cut small: a plate trimmed too far looks like a scrap.
5. Tape the paper plate to the chest of the yellow t-shirt, centered like a face.
6. Gather the crew in a row for photos, keeping the paper plates taped flat so they do not swing.
7. Optional pro finish: outline the whole plate edge in black marker. The outline makes the face pop from across the room.

Q: How do you pick emojis for the crew?
A: Assign them first so nobody duplicates. Crowd-pleasers: heart-eyes, laughing-crying, and the sunglasses face. Let the shyest person take the poop emoji: it gets the biggest laugh.

Q: How do you keep the plate from swinging?
A: Tape it at four points, top, bottom, and both sides, so it sits flat on the chest. Two tape points lets it flap all night.

### Emotion Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emotion-crew

One loud color per person: each of you is a different emotion.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 solid bright color outfit per person: yellow, blue, red, green, purple, or orange (buy: a set at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Face paint matching each outfit color, 1 per person (buy: drugstore)
- 1 white poster board per person (buy: dollar store)
- Markers, 1 set (make: from the house)
- Colored hair spray matching each outfit, 1 can per person, optional (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Pull one loud solid-color outfit per person from the closet. Buy the face paint, poster board, and markers.
2. Each person picks an emotion and writes it big on poster board: Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear, Disgust, Anxiety, Envy, Embarrassment, Ennui.
3. Paint a simple face design in the matching color: a big smile, a tear, furrowed brows. Mist hair with the matching color spray if you like.
4. Wear the full monochrome outfit with the emotion sign. Group up in a row like the control panel.
5. Optional pro finish: paint each face design in the matching outfit color only, one color per person. Mixed colors muddy the read; monochrome reads as a character.

Q: How do you stop two people picking the same emotion?
A: Assign emotions before anyone shops: Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear, Disgust, Anxiety, Envy, Embarrassment, Ennui. First come first served, written on a list.

Q: How big should the emotion sign be?
A: Letter it 4 inches tall minimum on the poster board. The sign is the costume's label: if nobody can read it across the room, it is decoration.

### Emotional Support Dinosaur

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/emotional-support-dinosaur

Dino-spike vest over normal clothes with a badge that says Emotional Support Dinosaur. Do not pet.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 15 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 vest or sleeveless jacket you own (own)
- 1 sheet green craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- 1 blank badge or pin (buy: office supply aisle)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Marker, 1
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut one paper spike first and hold it against the vest shoulder to check the size, about 3 inches tall.
2. Cut 6 to 8 triangle spikes from the green craft felt with the scissors using the paper template. Uniform spikes look designed; freehand spikes look ragged.
3. Glue the spikes along the vest shoulders and back. Let dry 15 minutes.
4. Write 'Emotional Support Dinosaur. Do not pet.' on the badge with the marker.
5. Pin it on and refuse all pets.
6. Optional pro finish: write 'Emotional Support Dinosaur' in all caps on the badge, then add 'Do not pet.' underneath in smaller letters. The official-looking hierarchy sells the joke.

Q: Will fabric glue hold spikes through a night of hugs?
A: Yes if you glue the night before so it cures fully. Same-day glue is still tacky by party time and spikes slide.

Q: What vest works best?
A: Any vest or sleeveless jacket with structured shoulders: denim, fleece, or utility. Floppy vests let the spikes droop.

### Enchanted Castle Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/enchanted-castle-crew

The bookish princess, the cursed prince, the talking candelabra, the talking clock, the talking teapot: pick your role.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Princess: yellow fabric, 2 yards (buy: fabric store)
- Prince: 1 blue jacket and 1 pair dark pants (make: use your closet)
- Candelabra: gold face paint, 1 tube, and 1 gold headband (buy: craft store)
- Clock: 1 brown cardboard circle, about 12 inches, and painted hands (make: from a box)
- Teapot: 1 white pot or cardboard pot body (make: from a box)
- Hot glue gun, 1; scissors, 1 pair; face paint, 1 set

Steps:
1. Princess: wrap and pin the yellow fabric as a simple gown. Prince: wear the blue jacket and dark pants with a sash of torn fabric.
2. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue, and keep the face paint away from the eyes.
3. Cut three flame shapes from cardboard first and arrange them dry on the gold headband to check the spacing.
4. Glue them with the hot glue. Hot glue sets in seconds and cannot be repositioned, so the dry layout is the whole step.
5. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the cardboard.
6. Clock: paint the brown cardboard circle cream and add painted hands. Teapot: cut a rounded cardboard pot body, add a handle and spout, and wear it over the shoulders.
7. Optional pro finish: add a red fabric sash to the prince's blue jacket. The sash is the one detail that turns jacket-and-pants into royalty.

Q: How do you assign roles without fights?
A: Assign before shopping: princess, prince, candelabra, clock, teapot. Write them on a list and let the youngest pick first.

Q: How do you keep the teapot body on?
A: Cut arm holes in the cardboard pot body and wear it like a vest over the shoulders. A body with no arm holes slides off by the second photo.

### Error 404

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/error-404

Wear all black with a blank white page taped to your chest; carry a phone with a cracked-screen prop.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 black hoodie (make: use your closet)
- 1 pair black pants (make: use your closet)
- 1 sheet white paper, blank (make: use what you own)
- 1 old phone case or cracked-screen phone protector prop (make: use an old case)
- Tape, 1 roll (make: use what you own)

Steps:
1. Put on the black hoodie and black pants.
2. Tape a blank sheet of white paper to the front of the hoodie, taping all four corners.
3. Put the cracked-screen protector or old case on the phone and hold it as if it is still loading.
4. When asked about the costume, point to the blank page and announce that the costume cannot be found.
5. Freeze whenever someone talks to you, then reload.
6. Optional pro finish: let the tape job look slapdash. The messy tape is part of the joke.

Q: How does the paper stay on?
A: Tape all four corners of the paper to the hoodie. Tape sticks to fleece well enough for one evening and peels off after.

Q: Why is the paper blank?
A: The blank page is the whole joke: a real 404 has nothing to load. Writing on it just spoils it.

### Extinct Party Animal

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/extinct-party-animal

Felt dino spikes on a normal jacket, plus a party hat and a badge that reads Last seen 66 million years ago.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 15 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 jacket or blazer you own (own)
- 1 sheet green craft felt, 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- 1 party hat (buy: dollar store or party aisle)
- 1 blank name badge (buy: office supply aisle)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Marker, 1
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut one paper spike first and check the size against the jacket shoulder, about 3 inches tall.
2. Cut 6 to 8 triangle spikes from the green craft felt with the scissors. Cut them all from the template so the row looks even.
3. Glue the spikes in a row along the shoulders of the jacket. Let dry 15 minutes.
4. Write 'Last seen 66 million years ago' on the badge with the marker.
5. Pin on the badge, put on the party hat, and work the room.
6. Optional pro finish: write 'Last seen 66 million years ago' in neat block letters on the badge. Neat handwriting sells the museum-label joke; scribble kills it.

Q: Will the spikes survive on a blazer all night?
A: Yes if you glue them the night before and let the glue cure. Same-day glue peels when the jacket moves.

Q: How do you make the party hat stay on?

### Fairy Tale Princesses

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/fairy-tale-princesses

A dress or a crown from the closet. Every princess works.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 dress from the closet per person (make: use what you own)
- 1 cereal box per crown (make: from a cereal box)
- Gold or silver paint or markers, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair and tape, 1 roll
- 1 hair ribbon per person (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Each princess picks any dress from her own closet.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the cardboard crowns.
3. Draw the crown shape on the cereal box in pencil first and hold it against the head to check the fit.
4. Cut the crown with the scissors, leaving a 1-inch tab to tape the ends together. Color it with the gold or silver paint or markers and let it dry.
5. Tie the hair ribbon as a bow, and tape the cardboard crown on top of the head.
6. Line up for a princess parade photo, and check that each cardboard crown sits snugly.
7. Optional pro finish: tie the ribbon as a bow under the crown, not on top. The bow peeking out below the crown looks styled; on top it looks like wrapping.

Q: How do you keep a cardboard crown on a kid's head?
A: Tape a bobby pin inside the crown and clip it to the hair. Crowns balanced on top slide off; pinned crowns survive the parade.

Q: Do the princesses need matching dresses?
A: No: any dress from the closet works, and different dresses look like different kingdoms. The crowns are what make it a group.

### Fossil Hunter

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/fossil-hunter

Khaki vest, toy brush, magnifying glass, and cardboard fossil bones in a belt pouch.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Khaki or tan vest with pockets, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Toy paintbrush or makeup brush, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Toy magnifying glass, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Cardboard for fossil bones, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Small canvas pouch or fanny pack, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Brown paper lunch bag, 1 (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Pencil, 1

Steps:
1. Draw bone shapes on the cardboard with the pencil: a femur, a rib, a skull. Keep them chunky, thin cardboard bones snap.
2. Cut the bones out with the scissors and shade the edges with the pencil for the dug-up look.
3. Tuck the cardboard bones into the pouch so the tops peek out.
4. Safety: Round all cardboard corners, and carry the brush bristles-down so nobody gets poked. Under 3: skip the bones and magnifying glass as carry props. Toddlers mouth everything and cardboard snaps. The vest and pouch alone carry the costume.
5. Wear the khaki vest over a plain shirt, the pouch on the belt, the brush in one pocket. Ages 3+: add the magnifying glass to the other pocket.
6. Optional pro finish: crumple the brown paper bag into a specimen bag and label it with the pencil. One labeled prop sells the whole expedition.

Q: How do you make cardboard bones look like fossils?
A: Cut them chunky, shade the edges with pencil, and rub a little dirt-colored eyeshadow into the surface. Uneven shading beats perfect coloring.

Q: What goes in the belt pouch?
A: The cardboard bones with their tops peeking out, plus the brush. A pouch that bulges with finds reads as a real dig kit.

### Fruit Salad Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/fruit-salad

Each person picks a fruit color, wears it head to toe with a leaf hat.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Solid-color outfits in fruit colors (red, yellow, green, orange), 1 set per person (buy: a set at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Green felt for leaf hats, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person (buy: craft store)
- Headbands, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Each person picks a fruit and wears that color head to toe. Red for strawberry, yellow for banana, green for lime, orange for orange.
2. Cut leaf shapes from green felt.
3. Glue one leaf to each headband and let it set fully before wearing. Glued leaves cannot be repositioned, so center each leaf on the band and press for 30 seconds.
4. Everyone wears their headband. Take a group photo as the fruit salad.
5. Optional pro finish: snip a center vein down each felt leaf with the scissors. The vein makes flat felt read as a real leaf in photos.

Q: How many fruits make a good salad?
A: Four to six. Three looks thin, more than six gets hard to photograph. Assign the biggest person the watermelon.

Q: How do you keep the leaf hats on?
A: Glue the leaf to the front-center of the headband and let it set fully. A leaf glued off-center flops forward all night.

### Fuzzy Gremlin Plush

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/fuzzy-gremlin

A furry brown onesie, big felt ears, and googly eyes.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Brown fuzzy onesie or footed pajamas, 1 (buy: thrift store or online)
- Brown craft felt, 2 sheets 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Large googly eyes, 2 (buy: craft store)
- White felt for teeth, 1 small piece (buy: craft store)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut two big round ears from the brown felt and glue them to the onesie hood.
2. Glue the googly eyes to the forehead of the hood, above the face opening.
3. Glue two small white felt triangles under the hood edge as teeth.
4. Safety: Glue the eyes to the hood, never near the child's face, and keep all small parts where little hands cannot pull them off.
5. Optional pro finish: carry the gremlin in a laundry basket for arrivals. The unboxing gets the biggest reaction.

Q: How do you keep the big ears from flopping?
A: Glue each ear to a cardboard circle first, then glue the circles to the hood. The cardboard is the skeleton.

Q: What if the onesie is not fuzzy?
A: A brown sweatsuit works. The ears and eyes carry the costume, not the fabric texture.

### Fuzzy Monster

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/fuzzy-monster

A pastel fuzzy sweatsuit with giant googly eyes and an oversized stitched smile.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 pastel fuzzy sweatsuit (buy: discount store)
- 2 large googly eyes, 3 inches or bigger (buy: craft store; paper circles work too)
- 1 sheet white felt, 9x12 inches, for the smile (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Fabric glue, 1 tube, or 4 safety pins

Steps:
1. Glue or pin the two googly eyes to the hood of the pastel fuzzy sweatsuit.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the white felt.
3. Draw the smile on paper first and hold it against the sweatsuit chest to check the size: it should span most of the chest.
4. Cut the stitched-style smile from the white felt with the scissors. Cut it bigger than feels right: small smiles disappear into the fuzz.
5. Let the fabric glue dry fully before wearing.
6. Wear the hood up so the googly eyes sit above the forehead.
7. Optional pro finish: cut two small felt fangs and glue them at the smile's corners. Fangs turn a friendly monster into a funny one.

Q: Googly eyes or paper circles for the eyes?
A: Googly eyes photograph ten times better. Paper circles work too, but they curl in humidity.

Q: Will the eyes stay on the hood?
A: Glue them the night before so the fabric glue cures, or pin them with two safety pins each. Same-day glue plus a bouncing kid equals lost eyes.

### Galaxy Knights

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/galaxy-knights

Robes, belts, and toy energy blades for knights of a far-off galaxy.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 brown or beige bathrobe or long coat per knight (make: from closet)
- 1 toy energy-blade prop per knight (buy: toy store)
- 1 wide belt or rope sash per knight (make: from closet)
- 1 pair dark pants and boots per knight (make: from closet)
- Brown face paint for a hood shadow, 1 tube, optional (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Wear the bathrobe over dark pants with the belt tied at the waist. Pull the hood up.
2. Carry the energy blade unlit until the photo. Two stances: blade up ready, or blade down calm.
3. Safety: Keep the toy blades pointed up or down, never at faces. Sparring stays slow and pretend.
4. Line up the knights in a row, ignite the blades, and take the council photo.
5. Optional pro finish: tie the belt over the robe at the natural waist and let the robe flare below it. Belted robes read as uniform; unbelted robes read as bath time.

Q: Are toy energy blades safe for kids?
A: Yes if they are soft foam or plastic with rounded tips. Keep blades pointed up or down, never at faces, and skip hard plastic for kids under 6.

Q: How do you make a bathrobe not look like a bathrobe?
A: Belt it tight at the waist, pull the hood up, and wear dark pants and boots underneath. The belt and the boots do all the work.

### Garden Fairy

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/garden-fairy

Tulle wings, a flower crown, and a wand: the backyard turns into a fairy tale.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Pink tulle, 1 yard (buy: craft store)
- Cardboard for wings, 1 large piece about 2x3 feet (make: from a shipping box)
- Fake flowers, 1 bunch (buy: dollar store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store, or own)
- Wooden dowel or stick for the wand, about 12 inches (make: from the yard)
- Cardboard star for the wand tip, 1 (make: from scraps)
- Elastic for wing straps, about 2 feet (buy: craft store)
- Glitter glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Glue, 1 bottle
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Draw ONE wing on paper, cut it, and trace it flipped for the second. Symmetric wings are the fairy illusion. Cut two large wing shapes from the cardboard with the scissors.
2. Cover each wing with pink tulle and tape the edges down.
3. Glue fake flowers around the headband for the crown.
4. Tape the cardboard star to the top of the dowel for the wand.
5. Safety: Keep the wand away from faces during photos.
6. Tape elastic straps to the back of the wings and slip arms through.
7. Optional pro finish: outline the wing edges with glitter glue and add three dots down the center. The glitter edge catches light in every photo.

Q: How do you keep cardboard wings from flopping?
A: Score a center crease and tape a ruler or paint stick along the back as a spine. Flat cardboard folds; spined cardboard holds.

Q: What is the fastest fairy wand?
A: A stick with a star cut from cardboard, glittered, taped on. Five minutes, and every fairy photo needs the wand.

### Garden Gnome

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/garden-gnome

Wear earth tones, make a pointy hat from cardboard, draw a white beard, carry a tiny fishing rod or garden shovel.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Earth-tone shirt and pants, 1 set (own)
- Cardboard for the hat, 1 sheet (make: from a box)
- Blue paint for the hat, 1 small bottle (buy: craft store)
- White face paint for the beard, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- Toy fishing rod or small garden shovel, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Tape, 1 roll

Steps:
1. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the cardboard.
2. Cut the sheet cardboard to size, roll it into a tall cone, and tape it shut.
3. Paint the cone with the blue paint for the hat, and let it dry.
4. Test the face paint on the inside of the wrist first and wait 10 minutes, kids' skin reacts more than you expect.
5. Use the brown and black non-toxic face paint to draw a round nose and rosy cheeks. Keep all paint clear of the eyes and mouth.
6. Wear the cone hat with the earth-tone shirt and pants, and carry the toy fishing rod.
7. Optional pro finish: carry a tiny watering can or a foam mushroom. Gnomes have props, the hat and beard say gnome, the watering can says garden gnome.

Q: How tall should the gnome hat be?
A: About as tall as the head. Too short reads as a party hat; too tall flops. Roll the cone, tape it, and test the height before painting.

Q: Will the face-paint beard smear?
A: Let it dry fully before the hat goes on, and keep it below the mouth. Bring the tube for touch-ups; white shows every smudge.

### Ghost Hunters

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ghost-hunters

Khaki jumpsuits, cardboard ghost-catching backpacks, name patches.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 khaki or tan jumpsuit, or matching shirt and pants, per person (buy: thrift store)
- 1 small cardboard box per person, shoebox size (make: use what you own)
- White paper, 2 sheets, and markers for name patches (make: use what you own)
- 1 sheet black cardboard per person (make: from a box)
- Packing tape or glue, scissors

Steps:
1. Tape the small cardboard box shut for the backpack.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the black cardboard.
3. Draw the straps, dial, and hose shapes on the black cardboard with marker first and hold them against the box to check the size.
4. Cut them with the scissors. Cut the hose shape last and widest: it is the most visible piece.
5. Mark each last name on the white paper with the markers. Tape it to the chest as a name patch.
6. Wear the backpack over the jumpsuit, and keep the box small and light so kids can wear it all night.
7. Optional pro finish: write each person's last name on the white paper patch in block letters and tape it to the chest. The name patch is the detail that turns khaki clothes into a uniform.

Q: How do you keep the backpack box light enough for kids?
A: Use a small box, shoebox size max, and tape it shut empty. Kids wear it all night only if it weighs almost nothing.

Q: How do you attach the box to the back?
A: Tape two ribbon straps to the box like a backpack. Tape alone on the shirt peels; straps distribute the weight.

### Gloom & Bloom

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/gloom-bloom

Braids and black for Gloom, color-pop and smiles for Bloom.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 set black clothes from the closet (make: use what you own)
- 1 set colorful clothes from the closet (make: use what you own)
- Black and white face paint, non-toxic, 1 set (buy: drugstore)
- 2 hair ties for braids (make: use what you own)
- 3 to 5 fake flowers (buy: dollar store; paper flowers work too)

Steps:
1. Gloom: wear the black clothes, and braid the hair tightly with the hair ties.
2. Paint a small black teardrop under one eye with the black and white face paint.
3. Bloom: wear the colorful clothes, and pin the fake flowers in the hair.
4. Paint a small flower on one cheek with the face paint, keeping it clear of the eyes.
5. Stand side by side: Gloom frowns and looks away, Bloom smiles big.
6. Optional pro finish: braid the gloom hair tight with a middle part, and pin the bloom flowers all on one side. Opposite styling is what makes the pair read as opposites.

Q: How do you paint a teardrop that does not smear?
A: Paint it small under one eye with a thin brush, not a finger, and let it set before touching the face. Fingers smudge; brushes stay sharp.

Q: What makes the pair read as a duo?
A: The contrast: one frowns and looks away, one smiles big. Pose the attitude, not just the clothes.

### Glow Skeleton

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/glow-skeleton

Black sweats with glow-in-the-dark bone tape, plus glow bracelets.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black sweatsuit, 1 (buy: discount store, or own)
- Glow-in-the-dark bone tape, 1 roll (buy: craft store)
- Glow bracelets, 1 pack (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Black face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Charge the bone tape under a lamp for 20 minutes for maximum glow.
2. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the bone tape.
3. Cut the bone tape into rib bones: lay strips horizontally across the chest and back. Add vertical spine segments down the center, and arm and leg bones down the limbs.
4. Snap the glow bracelets onto both wrists and both ankles right before heading out.
5. Test the face paint on the wrist first and wait 10 minutes for any reaction. Paint simple skull eye circles with the black face paint, keeping clear of the eyes so vision stays clear.
6. Safety: Under 3: skip the glow bracelets, toddlers can chew them open and they are small parts. Skip the skull face paint too, little kids rub their eyes and the glow tape alone carries the costume.
7. Optional pro finish: 'charge' the glow tape under a bright lamp for 10 minutes right before heading out. Freshly charged tape glows dramatically for the first hour, that is when the photos happen.
8. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: Does glow tape really glow all night?
A: No, it fades over 1 to 2 hours. Charge it under bright light right before going out, and bring the roll for touch-ups. The first hour is the magic hour.

Q: Tape or paint for the bones?
A: Tape. It is faster, cleaner, peels off after, and actually glows. Painted bones look better in daylight but vanish at night, which defeats the costume.

### Goggle Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/goggle-crew

Yellow tees, denim overalls, goggles, black gloves.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 yellow t-shirt per person (buy: craft store, or use one you own)
- 1 pair denim overalls per person (buy: thrift store, or use one you own)
- 1 pair swim or safety goggles per person (buy: toy store)
- 1 pair black gloves per person (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Each person puts on the yellow t-shirt, the denim overalls, and the black gloves.
2. Push the goggles up on the forehead like safety gear, not over the eyes, so everyone can see.
3. Walk in a pack and greet people in gibberish for the full effect.
4. Skip any real tools or hard hats so the look stays clearly costume, not work gear.
5. Optional pro finish: push the goggles up on the forehead, never over the eyes. Forehead goggles are the character's signature; over the eyes you just look like a swimmer.

Q: Do the overalls have to be denim?
A: Denim reads best, but any overalls work. The yellow shirt plus goggles carry the costume; the overalls are the bonus.

Q: How do you do the voice without annoying everyone?
A: Keep the gibberish to greetings and photos, then talk normally. Full-time gibberish is funny for ten minutes and exhausting by hour two.

### Good Witch, Bad Witch

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/good-witch-bad-witch

Green face paint and black for one, pink gown and crown for the other.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 black dress or set of black clothes for the bad witch (make: use your closet)
- 1 pink dress or set of pink clothes for the good witch (make: use your closet)
- Green face paint, non-toxic, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- 1 cardboard crown (make: from a cereal box)
- 1 black cone hat (buy: dollar store)
- Hot glue gun, scissors, 1 pink marker, tape

Steps:
1. Bad witch: wear the black dress or black clothes.
2. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue, and keep the green face paint away from the eyes.
3. Test the hat brim bend dry before gluing: fold the brim, check it in a mirror, then hot glue it. Hot glue sets in seconds and cannot be repositioned.
4. Paint the bad witch's face and hands green with the green face paint, keeping paint away from the eyes and patch-testing sensitive skin first.
5. Good witch: wear the pink dress or pink clothes. Color the cardboard crown with the pink marker, and tape it on the head.
6. Optional pro finish: color the cardboard crown with the pink marker on both sides. A double-sided crown flashes pink in photos; single-sided flashes brown cardboard.

Q: How do you get green face paint off kids?
A: Wash with gentle cleanser and soap the same night, not just water. Green needs soap. Moisturize after and never let them sleep in it.

Q: What if the cone hat will not stay on?
A: Tape a bobby pin inside the hat and clip it to the hair. Cone hats are top-heavy and slide without an anchor.

### Goth Girl with Braids

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/goth-braids

Black dress, two tight braids, and a stare that ends conversations.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black dress, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Black tights, 1 pair (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Hair ties, 2 (own)
- Black eyeliner, 1 (own, or buy: drugstore)
- Pale foundation or white face paint, 1 (buy: drugstore or craft store)
- Dark lipstick, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Pull the hair into two tight braids, one behind each ear, and tie them off.
2. Apply the pale foundation lightly, then heavy black eyeliner.
3. Wear the black dress with black tights and dark lipstick.
4. Safety: Test the face paint on the inside of the wrist first and wash it off before bed so it never stains the pillow.
5. Practice the stare in the mirror: calm, unimpressed, unblinking.
6. Optional pro finish: carry a black umbrella even if it is not raining. The prop completes the silhouette.
7. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: How do you keep the braids tight all night?
A: Braid damp hair and tie each braid at two points, top and bottom. Damp braids set tighter as they dry.

Q: What if the dress is not quite black enough?
A: A very dark gray or navy reads black in party lighting. The braids and makeup carry the costume either way.

---

### Haunted Animatronics

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/haunted-animatronics

Glitchy mascot heads from cardboard boxes, flickering LED eyes, jerky moves.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- 1 large cardboard box per person, big enough to cover the head (make: use what you own)
- 2 red LED tea lights per person (buy: dollar store)
- Paint in gray, black, and one accent color, 1 small bottle each (buy: craft store)
- 1 set old clothes with holes or tears (make: use what you own)
- Hot glue gun, 1; scissors, 1 pair; utility knife, 1 (adults only)

Steps:
1. Safety: An adult handles the utility knife and the hot glue for every cut and glue step.
2. Mark the eye holes and the wide jagged mouth on the OUTSIDE of the box first, then have the wearer hold the box up to check the eye placement before any cutting.
3. Cut with the utility knife, adults only, cutting the eye holes generous and the mouth wide. Cardboard cut away cannot be put back, and small eye holes make a blind hazard.
4. Paint the box gray with black scuffs and cracks. Glue one red LED tea light inside each eye hole.
5. Safety: Make the eye holes large, and never wear the box near stairs or traffic, since side vision is limited.
6. Wear the box over the head with the eyes lined up to the holes. Wear the old clothes with holes underneath, and move in short jerky steps, freezing between moves.
7. Optional pro finish: paint black scuffs and cracks around the eye holes before adding the lights. The damage detail is what reads as haunted instead of just boxy.

Q: How do you see out of a box on your head?
A: Cut the eye holes large and line your eyes up to them before the paint goes on. Never wear it near stairs or traffic: side vision is almost zero.

Q: How do the red eyes stay lit all night?
A: LED tea lights run 24 hours plus on one battery. Tape one inside each eye hole with the light facing out, and carry a spare set just in case.

### Haunted Portraits

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/haunted-portraits

Gray makeup, old-timey clothes, hold a gilt frame.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- 1 set old-fashioned dark clothes per person, e.g. a vest, long skirt, or button-up (make: use your closet)
- Gray and white face paint, non-toxic, 1 set (buy: drugstore)
- 1 large picture frame or cardboard frame per person (buy: thrift store for the frame, or make from cardboard)
- Hair spray or powder for a grayed look, 1 (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Paint each face pale gray with white highlights on the cheekbones and nose, using the gray and white face paint.
2. Gray the hair with the hair powder.
3. Dress in the old-fashioned dark clothes from the closet.
4. Hold the picture frame or cardboard frame up around the face like a living portrait.
5. Pose together in a row of frames for group photos, keeping the face paint light around the eyes.
6. Optional pro finish: dust the hair with the gray powder and add white highlights on the cheekbones and nose. The highlights are what read as painted portrait instead of just pale.

Q: How do you hold the frame up all night?
A: You do not: use it for photos only, and set it down between shots. Holding a frame for hours is exhausting; the portrait pose is a photo bit.

Q: How do you gray the face without looking dirty?
A: Paint the face pale gray, not dark, and add white highlights on the cheekbones and nose. Dark gray reads as dirt; pale gray with highlights reads as a painting.

### Headless Horsemen

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/headless-horsemen

Black capes, jack-o-lanterns held at shoulder height, group gallop.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Black cape or black sheet, 1 per person (buy: dollar store, or own: black sheet)
- Small jack-o-lantern bucket or foam pumpkin, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Broom or stick-horse substitute, 1 per person (own: broom from home)
- Tape, 1 roll (own)
- Glow bracelets, 1 pack (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Drape the black cape or black sheet over the shoulders.
2. Safety: Keep your real head tucked low so you can see the ground.
3. Tuck the chin into the chest, and hold the jack-o-lantern bucket up at shoulder height like a carried head.
4. Add a glow bracelet to each wrist so drivers can see you in the dark.
5. Hold the broom between the legs like a horse, and gallop in a group line.
6. Optional pro finish: put a battery tea light inside each jack-o-lantern bucket. A glowing 'head' reads from a block away and keeps the group visible.

Q: How does the rider see if their head is tucked?
A: Tuck the chin but keep the eyes looking forward under the cape edge, the cape drapes like a hood, it does not cover the face. If vision is blocked at all, ditch the tuck and just carry the bucket high.

Q: What do we use if we have no capes?
A: Black trash bags with head and arm holes cut out, or any dark blanket. The silhouette is what matters: dark shoulders plus a glowing pumpkin at head height.

### Hero Squad

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/hero-squad

Color-coded capes and masks, one team pose for photos.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Cape per person in squad colors, 1 each (buy: craft store, or make: cut from 1 yard of fabric each)
- Mask per person matching the cape color, 1 each (buy: craft store)
- T-shirt per person in the cape color, 1 each (buy: craft store)
- Fabric paint for the team emblem, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 2 per person (own)

Steps:
1. Sketch the team emblem on scrap paper and have the whole squad approve it BEFORE opening the paint, painted emblems cannot be unpainted.
2. Then each hero paints the same emblem, like a lightning bolt, on the t-shirt with the fabric paint.
3. Let the fabric paint dry fully before wearing.
4. Safety: Keep each cape short enough to clear the ground so nobody trips.
5. Pin each cape at the shoulders with a safety pin, and wear the matching mask.
6. End every appearance with the team pose: fists on hips, capes billowing.
7. Optional pro finish: paint a matching emblem on each cape near the shoulder. Capes with emblems look designed; plain capes look borrowed.

Q: How long does the fabric paint take to dry?
A: About 1 to 2 hours to stop being tacky, overnight to be safe. Paint the shirts the night before the event or the emblem smears when worn.

Q: How do you keep capes safe for small kids?
A: Keep each cape short enough to clear the ground, and pin them with safety pins instead of tying, pinned capes pull free if snagged. Never tie a cape tight around a small child's neck.

### Hot Dog

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/hot-dog

Tan foam pool noodle bun, red shirt for the dog, mustard squiggle.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red t-shirt, 1 (own)
- Tan or beige foam pool noodle, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Yellow fabric paint for mustard, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins or fabric glue, 1 pack (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Put on the red shirt. You are the hot dog.
2. Cut the pool noodle in half lengthwise to make two bun halves.
3. Paint a thin mustard squiggle down one bun half with the yellow fabric paint. You can always add more paint, but you cannot remove it, so start thin. Let dry fully before attaching.
4. Attach the bun halves to your sides with safety pins or fabric glue, one on each side.
5. Optional pro finish: add a white paper vendor hat. The hat turns 'person in a bun' into a ballpark vendor, and vendors get offered tips.

Q: How do you make the bun halves stay on the shoulders?
A: Pin each half at the shoulder seam with two safety pins from inside the shirt. They sit like epaulettes, stable all night, no glue on skin.

Q: Ketchup and mustard or just mustard?
A: Both, in zigzag squiggles. The zigzag is the visual shorthand for condiments, straight lines read as stripes, zigzags read as sauce.

### Ice Cream Cone

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ice-cream-cone

A tan paper cone hat and a sprinkle-dotted scoop shirt.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Tan paper party hat or cone, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- White t-shirt, 1 (buy: craft store, or use one you own)
- Colored dot stickers or pom-poms for sprinkles, 1 pack (buy: craft store; cut paper dots work too)
- Brown paint or marker for the cone crosshatch, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Tape, 1 roll (own)

Steps:
1. Draw a waffle-cone crosshatch on the tan paper party hat with the brown marker.
2. Set the tan paper party hat on the head like a hat, and tape the elastic so it sits snugly.
3. Safety: Keep small pom-poms away from kids under three, since they are a choking hazard.
4. Cover the white t-shirt with the colored dot stickers or pom-poms, scattered like sprinkles. Keep the stickers off the skin.
5. Optional pro finish: add a red pom-pom 'cherry' to the tip of the hat with a dot of glue. The cherry is what makes strangers say the flavor out loud.

Q: How do you keep the cone hat on all night?
A: Tape the hat's elastic strap so it fits snug under the chin, and add a second piece of tape inside the hat brim. Paper hats are light; they fall off because the elastic is loose, not because of wind.

Q: Pom-poms or stickers for the sprinkles?
A: Stickers for under-5s (no choking risk, nothing falls off). Pom-poms photograph better but shed all night and are a choking hazard for toddlers.

### Ice Skater

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ice-skater

A white dress, tights, and a perfect bun: gold-medal energy, no ice required.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- White dress, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own)
- White tights, 1 pair (own, or buy: clothing store)
- Hair donut for the bun, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Blush, 1 (own, or buy: drugstore)
- Bobby pins, 1 pack (own)

Steps:
1. Buy or pull the white dress, white tights, and hair donut.
2. Twist the hair into a high bun around the hair donut and pin it.
3. Dab a little blush on the cheeks for the cold-air glow.
4. Safety: Skip real skates; this costume is for dry land only.
5. Wear the white dress with the tights and strike the finishing pose.
6. Optional pro finish: wrap white ribbon crisscrossed up the calves over the tights. The laced calves read as skates even in sneakers.

Q: No ice skates, what goes on the feet?
A: White sneakers or white boots. Nobody sees feet past the laced calves; the ribbon lacing does the work.

Q: How do you get the perfect skater bun?
A: A hair donut plus bobby pins, twist the hair around the donut and pin every inch. The donut is the difference between a bun and a lump.

### Juke-Joint Vampires

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/juke-joint-vampires

Sharp vintage suits, fangs, and a trumpet one of you never puts down.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Vintage-style suits, 2 (buy: thrift store)

- Plastic vampire fangs, 2 sets (buy: dollar store or costume aisle)
- Fake blood, 1 bottle (buy: costume aisle)

Steps:

### Kart Racers

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/kart-racers

Cardboard karts and racing caps for a full starting grid of friends.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Large cardboard box, 1 per racer, big enough to fit around the torso (make: collect spares)
- Red, blue, green, and yellow paint or wrapping paper, 1 bottle or roll per color (buy: dollar store)
- Paper plates for wheels, 4 per kart (buy: dollar store)
- Racing cap or helmet, 1 per person (own: from closet)
- Scissors, 1 pair, tape, 1 roll, and string, 1 spool (own: household tools)
- Ribbon for kart straps, about 3 feet per kart (own: from closet)

Steps:
1. Have each racer step inside the box first and mark where the waist sits BEFORE cutting, an opening cut too big slides down, and cardboard cut away cannot be put back.
2. Cut the top and bottom out of each box so it fits around the torso like a kart, starting with a smaller opening and widening. Paint each kart a different bright color.
3. Tape two paper-plate wheels to each side. Tape ribbon straps inside so the kart hangs at waist height.
4. Safety: Keep the kart box at waist height so legs move freely, and tape all cut edges smooth.
5. Wear the kart with the racing cap, line up side by side, and strike the starting-grid pose.
6. Optional pro finish: number each kart with a big marker digit on the front. Numbered karts turn a row of boxes into a starting grid.

Q: How do you wear a cardboard kart without tripping?
A: Keep the box at waist height with the ribbon straps, and keep the bottom opening wide enough that legs move freely. Tape all cut edges smooth so cardboard never scratches thighs.

Q: Paint or wrapping paper for the kart color?
A: Wrapping paper is faster and has zero drying time; paint looks better up close. For kids, wrapping paper wins, they can help tape it on.

### Ketchup & Mustard

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ketchup-mustard

Red bottle tunic and cap for one, yellow for the other.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- 1 red t-shirt, 1 yellow t-shirt (make: raid the closet)
- Red felt or construction paper, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, or use paper from home)
- Yellow felt or construction paper, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, or use paper from home)
- Safety pins, 8 (buy: dollar store, or raid the sewing kit)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Pick who is ketchup (red shirt) and who is mustard (yellow shirt). No wrong answer, but decide before you start cutting, it avoids the only argument this costume can cause.
2. Cut a big blob shape from the red paper, about the size of a dinner plate. Round the edges; a neat circle reads as a sticker, a blob reads as a squeeze of ketchup.
3. Cut a matching blob from the yellow paper.
4. Pin the red blob to the yellow shirt and the yellow blob to the red shirt with 4 safety pins each, pinned from inside. Each person wears the OTHER condiment's color, that is the joke.
5. Optional pro finish: write the nutrition facts on the back of each shirt with a marker ('Serving size: 1 awesome couple'). People will turn you around to read it.
6. Safety: Pin from inside the shirt so no pin backs touch skin, and keep the pins flat, nobody wants a poke during a hug.
7. Stand side by side and take the photo. The internet has decided this is a top-10 couples costume; you are now contractually obligated to look delighted.

Q: How do you keep the paper blobs from tearing?
A: Pin from inside the shirt with four pins each, and use felt instead of paper if it might rain. Felt survives weather; paper does not.

Q: Why does each person wear the other condiment's color?
A: That is the joke, ketchup wears mustard's blob and mustard wears ketchup's. Same-color blobs would just be two people in colored shirts.

### Pop Star Demon Huntresses

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/kpop-demon-huntresses

Matching stage outfits, toy microphones, and demon-hunter poses for three.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 10 min drying / Medium

Materials:

- Toy microphones, 3 (buy: dollar store)
- Cardboard for swords, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Silver duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Face paint in purple and black, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Hair gel, 1 (own)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Agree on one accent color for all three outfits so the trio reads as a unit.
2. Cut three sword shapes from the cardboard and wrap the blades in silver duct tape.
3. Dress each hunter in black pants, a metallic top, and bold face paint stripes.
4. Safety: Keep the cardboard swords light and never swing them near faces in a crowd.
5. Practice one shared pose, microphones up, swords crossed, and hit it for every photo.
6. Optional pro finish: paint matching symbols on the back of each hand. The matching marks sell the team.

Q: How do you keep three outfits matching without buying new clothes?
A: One shared accent color plus matching face paint unifies any three black outfits. The audience reads the trio, not the labels.

Q: What if we only have two people?

### Ladybug

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ladybug

Red sweats, black felt dots, and little spotted wings.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red shirt, 1 (own)
- Black pants, 1 pair (own)
- Black felt for dots, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Black pipe cleaners for antennae, 2 (buy: craft store)
- Black pom-poms, 2 small (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Cut lots of circles from the black felt with the scissors.
2. Arrange all the dots on the shirt DRY first and step back to check, dots cluster in the middle if you glue as you go.
3. Cut 8 to 10 black felt circles with the scissors, arrange them spread across the red shirt, then glue.
4. Cut two small wing shapes from the felt scraps, dot them, and pin them at the back.
5. Bend pipe cleaners into antennae and attach them to the headband.
6. Safety: Pin the wings where little hands cannot reach the pins.
7. Wear the dotted sweats with the antennae headband.
8. Optional pro finish: paint a black center line down the back of the shirt with fabric paint. The center line splits the wings, without it, the dots read as polka dots, not ladybug.

Q: How many dots does a ladybug need?
A: Seven is the classic (like the seven-spotted ladybug), but 8 to 10 spread evenly photographs better. Odd numbers look natural; even numbers look patterned.

Q: How do you keep felt dots on through the night?
A: Fabric glue applied the night before, or safety pins from inside for day-of. Tape peels by hour two, do not trust tape.

### Little Artist

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-artist

A beret, a cardboard paint palette, and a splatter-painted smock.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Beret or flat cap, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Cardboard for the palette, 1 piece (make: from a shipping box)
- Washable paint set, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Old smock or oversized t-shirt, 1 (own)
- Paintbrush, 1 (own, or buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Draw the kidney-bean palette shape on the cardboard and check the size against the forearm BEFORE cutting. A palette cut too small looks like a toy. Cut it out with the scissors.
2. Paint dabs of bright color around the palette edge and let dry.
3. Flick a little paint onto the smock for splatters and let dry.
4. Safety: Use washable paint only; cover the table before splattering.
5. Wear the smock and the tilted beret, and carry the palette and brush.
6. Optional pro finish: squeeze real paint dabs onto the cardboard palette and carry it. A palette with actual paint on it is the prop that makes strangers say 'oh, an artist!' instead of 'nice beret.'

Q: How do you keep the beret on a small head?
A: Bobby-pin it at both temples, tilted to one side. Berets slide straight back without pins, the tilt plus pins locks it.

Q: What is on the cardboard palette?
A: Dabs of the same face paint colors, arranged in a circle. Match the palette to the cheek dabs and the costume tells one coherent story.

### Little Baker

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-baker

A paper chef hat, an apron, and a toy whisk.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- White paper or poster board for the hat, 2 sheets (buy: craft store, or use printer paper)
- Apron, 1 (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Toy whisk, 1 (buy: toy store or dollar store)
- Flour from the kitchen, 1 pinch (optional, for the effect)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1

Steps:
1. Roll the paper into a tall chef hat shape and tape the seam.
2. Measure the head with a paper strip BEFORE cutting. The hat band must fit snug or it slides over the eyes. Trim the hat band to fit the head with the scissors.
3. Safety: Keep real flour away from eyes; a tiny pinch on the apron only.
4. Wear the hat and the apron.
5. Carry the toy whisk and offer everyone imaginary cupcakes.
6. Optional pro finish: dust the apron with a little flour before heading out. One flour smudge is the difference between 'dressed as a baker' and 'is a baker.'

Q: Chef hat or baker hat, different?
A: Same hat, different props. Chefs carry the spoon; bakers carry the mixing bowl. The prop names the profession.

Q: How do you keep a paper hat on a toddler?
A: Elastic chin strap taped inside the band, loose enough for two fingers. Paper hats without straps last about four minutes on a toddler.

### Little Lifeguard

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-lifeguard

Red tee, whistle, and a rescue buoy made from a pool noodle ring: an everyday hero costume.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Plastic whistle on a lanyard, 1 (buy: dollar store or party store)
- Pool noodle, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- White duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Red shorts or swim trunks, 1 pair (own)
- White face paint stick for the nose stripe, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut the pool noodle with the scissors and curve it into a ring, taping the ends together with the white duct tape. An adult should do the cutting: pool noodles need firm pressure.
2. Wrap 4 white tape bands evenly around the ring so it reads as a rescue buoy.
3. Safety: The whistle is a photo prop the parent holds and brings out for pictures, not a blow-all-night toy.
4. Safety: The buoy is a costume prop, not a flotation device. Keep the lanyard short so it cannot catch on anything.
5. Wear the red tee and shorts and carry the buoy over one shoulder. The parent keeps the whistle and hands it over for photos.
6. Dab the white face paint stripe across the nose.
7. Optional pro finish: write LIFEGUARD across the back of the tee with the white duct tape in block letters. Back lettering is what strangers read first.

Q: How do you make the pool noodle ring stay round?
A: Cut the noodle ends at an angle so they meet in a clean joint, then wrap the joint with 3 layers of duct tape. The tape joint is stronger than the foam.

Q: Is a real whistle too loud for a kid costume?
A: One toot at a time is the rule. Party-store whistles are plenty loud; skip the metal coach whistles.

### Little Lion

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-lion

Tan sweatsuit plus a fuzzy mane hood.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Tan or brown sweatsuit, 1 (buy: discount store, or use one you own)
- Brown fuzzy fabric strip or old brown towel for the mane, about 24 inches long (buy: fabric store, or make: cut from a towel)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own)
- Safety pins or fabric glue, 6 to 8 pins or 1 tube glue (buy: dollar store or craft store)
- Brown non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Safety: Adults handle the scissors when cutting the brown fuzzy fabric.
2. Cut a paper collar template first and test it around the sweatsuit hood, a mane cut too small looks like a bib, and fuzzy fabric cut away cannot be put back.
3. Then cut the brown fuzzy fabric into a wide collar for the mane, cutting generous and trimming after the fitting.
4. Pin the mane around the hood or neckline of the tan sweatsuit with the safety pins, fluffing it outward.
5. Safety: Pin the mane from inside the sweatsuit, so pin backs face the fabric and never the skin.
6. Paint a brown nose and whiskers with the brown face paint, keeping clear of the eyes. Skip it for under-twos and any kid who rubs their face.
7. Pin the mane flat at the back so it does not slip over the eyes while the little lion runs.
8. Optional pro finish: cut a small triangle tail from the leftover fuzzy fabric and pin it to the back waistband. The tail is what other kids point at.

Q: How do you keep the mane out of the kid's face?
A: Pin the mane around the hood or neckline, not the forehead, and fluff it outward. Pin the back of the mane flat so it cannot slip forward over the eyes when they run.

Q: Safety pins or fabric glue for the mane?
A: Pins for anything a toddler wears, you can reposition them, and glue needs 30 minutes of stillness no toddler provides. Glue works fine for older kids who will sit still.

### Little Pig Family

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-pig-family

Pink clothes and a snout headband; little brother brings the dinosaur.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Pink t-shirts or pajamas, 1 per person (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Pink headband, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Pink paper cup, 1 per snout (own: from the kitchen drawer)
- Pink felt or construction paper, 2 triangles per ear (buy: craft store)
- Pink string or yarn, 1 arm length per snout (own: from the craft drawer)
- Scissors, 1 pair, and clear tape, 1 roll (own: household tools)
- Pink blush or face paint for cheeks, 1 (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Poke the holes SMALL first with the scissor tip and test the string fit, holes poked too big tear through the cup and the snout falls apart.
2. Poke two small holes in the sides of a pink paper cup.
3. Cut one paper ear template first and check the size on the headband, ears should stand about 3 inches tall.
4. Then cut two pink felt triangles with the scissors and tape them to the pink headband as ears.
5. Thread the pink string through the holes, then tie the cup gently in front of the nose.
6. Dab a little pink blush on each person's cheeks with a finger.
7. Hand the little brother a toy dinosaur from the toy store or one he owns. Now he is the pig who brings the dinosaur.
8. Optional pro finish: draw two small black nostril dots on the bottom of each cup snout with a marker. Nostrils are the detail that turns a taped cup into a snout.

Q: How do you tie the snout on without it hurting?
A: Thread the pink string through the holes and tie it loosely behind the head with a bow, never a knot. It should rest against the nose, not press into it, if it leaves a mark, it is too tight.

Q: The ears keep flopping on the headband. Fix?
A: Tape each triangle with a tab folded over the band on both sides, not just stuck on one side. The double-sided tab is what keeps felt ears upright.

### Little Prince

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-prince

Crown, cape, and a royal sash from the dress-up box or the craft drawer.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Gold cardstock or a paper crown, 1 (buy: party store, or make: from cardstock)
- Red or purple fabric for the cape, about 1 yard (own, or buy: craft store)
- Wide ribbon for the sash, about 2 yards (buy: craft store)
- Stick-on plastic gems, 1 pack (buy: dollar store)
- White gloves, 1 pair (buy: dollar store, optional)
- Safety pins, 2
- Scissors, 1 pair
- Glue stick, 1

Steps:
1. Cut the cardstock into a crown band sized to the head, overlap 1 inch, and glue. Cut triangle points along the top edge.
2. Press the stick-on gems around the crown band, one big gem centered on the front.
3. Drape the fabric as a cape.
4. For under-5s, skip the pins: tie the cape's top corners to the shirt shoulders with short ribbon ties, or glue the top edge to the back of the shirt. Nothing tied around the neck.
5. Safety: No pins near little hands. Keep the cape above the knees so it cannot trip. Nothing tied around the neck.
6. Sash: drape the wide ribbon from one shoulder to the opposite hip and tape or glue it at the waist.
7. Optional pro finish: tilt the crown slightly to one side. A crooked crown is the whole charm of a little prince.

Q: How do you keep a paper crown from tearing?
A: Use cardstock, not printer paper, and overlap the band a full inch before gluing. The stick-on gems add stiffness as a bonus.

Q: What if we have no cape fabric?
A: A red bath towel or a pillowcase works. Pin it at the shoulders, never tie it at the neck, and trim it above the knees.

---

### Little Shark

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-shark

Gray hoodie with a felt fin glued on the back.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Gray hoodie, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Gray felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- White felt, 1 small sheet (buy: craft store; white paper works too)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Cut a paper fin template first and hold it against the hoodie back, a fin cut too small disappears on the hoodie, and felt cut away cannot be put back.
2. Then cut a triangle fin about 8 inches tall from the gray felt, and a jagged row of teeth from the white felt.
3. Glue the teeth inside the hood edge of the gray hoodie so they show around the face.
4. Glue the fin to the back of the gray hoodie, low between the shoulders.
5. Let the fabric glue dry flat for 30 minutes.
6. Zip the gray hoodie over a white t-shirt and pull the hood up for the shark face.
7. Optional pro finish: glue two small black felt dots on the hood as eyes above the teeth. Eyes plus teeth is what makes it a shark face instead of a gray hood with trim.

Q: How do the teeth stay glued to the hood?
A: Fabric glue on the inside hood edge, pressed flat for 30 seconds per tooth, then left to dry flat for 30 minutes. Do not wear the hoodie until the glue is fully set or the teeth peel off.

Q: Where exactly does the fin go?
A: Low between the shoulders on the back, not up at the neck. A fin glued too high flops forward over the hood; low and centered stands upright when they walk.

---

### Little Witch

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/little-witch

Black cape, pointy hat, striped tights, green face paint.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black cape or black bedsheet, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: cut a cape from a black t-shirt)
- Pointy witch hat, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Black-and-white striped tights, 1 pair (buy: thrift store or online)
- Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: drugstore or craft store)
- Safety pin or ribbon, 1 (own: from the sewing kit)

Steps:
1. Pin the cape at the shoulders with the safety pin or tie it with ribbon.
2. Paint the nose, chin, and forehead lightly green with a fingertip or sponge. Use non-toxic kids' green face paint only.
3. Pull on the black-and-white striped tights and the pointy witch hat.
4. Carry a branch from the yard as a broom if one is handy.
5. Optional pro finish: tie the ribbon in a bow at the front of the cape instead of using a safety pin. A bow at the neck reads as costume; a visible safety pin reads as craft project.

Q: How much green face paint for a little witch?
A: Just the nose, chin, and forehead dabbed on lightly with a fingertip or sponge. A fully green face looks great for ten minutes and then smears on everything they touch.

Q: What if the cape is too long for a toddler?
A: Pin it at the shoulders so it hits mid-back, and trim the bottom if it still drags. A cape that reaches the ground on a small kid is a tripping hazard on stairs.

### Lost Tourist

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/lost-tourist

Wear wrinkled clothes, carry a crumpled map, add one luggage tag backwards on your shoulder.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- Button-down shirt, 1 (own, to wrinkle on purpose)
- Sunglasses and camera or phone on a strap, 1 set (own)
- Paper map, 1 (make: print one at home, or draw a fake map on printer paper)
- Luggage tag, 1 (buy: office supply store, or make: index card with string)
- Clear tape, 1 roll (own)

Steps:
1. Wrinkle the button-down shirt on purpose. Stuff it in a bag overnight, or ball it up and sit on it for ten minutes.
2. Write a fake name and hometown on an index card for the luggage tag. Punch a hole in the card and tie on the string.
3. Tape the luggage tag backwards on one shoulder with the clear tape so it faces the wrong way.
4. The map is the costume's punchline, fold it wrong-side-out and hold it upside down. A neatly folded map reads as prepared; an upside-down map reads as LOST. Commit to the upside-down.
5. Hang the camera or phone around the neck and put the sunglasses on top of the head.
6. Walk around looking at the map upside down.
7. Optional pro finish: ask strangers for directions to somewhere obvious, in character, all night. The costume is a performance, the map gets you noticed, the bit gets you remembered.

Q: What is the difference between Hawaiian shirt and lost tourist?
A: The map plus the confusion. Hawaiian shirt is a vibe; lost tourist is a character. Add the upside-down map and the asking-directions bit and it becomes a costume.

Q: Socks with sandals, really?
A: Really. It is the single most recognizable tourist signal on earth. White socks, sandals, confidence.

---

### Macabre Goth Couple

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/macabre-couple

Long black gown and calm stare for one, sharp suit for the other.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Long black dress or gown, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Black wig or black hair dye, 1 (buy: costume aisle)
- Pale foundation, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Dark lipstick, 1 (own)
- Black pinstripe or plain suit, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- White shirt, 1 (own)
- Black tie or cravat, 1 (buy: thrift store)

Steps:
1. She wears the long black gown with pale makeup and dark lips; he wears the suit with a stern expression.
2. Style the hair severe: slicked back for him, straight and long for her.
3. Walk arm in arm and speak as little as possible.
4. Safety: Test all makeup on a wrist first, and remove it fully before bed.
5. Never smile in photos. The unsmiling portrait is the entire aesthetic.
6. Optional pro finish: one shared prop, a black rose. The rose gives your hands something to do.

Q: How do you keep the look elegant instead of sloppy?
A: Fit matters more than fabric: tailor the thrifted pieces or pin them to fit. Sharp lines read expensive.

Q: What if the gown is too long?
A: Hem it to ankle length with iron-on tape. Floor-length gowns trip on stairs.

### Mermaid Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/mermaid-crew

The mermaid, the prince, the sea king, the sea witch, or the crab: pick your role.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- T-shirt or dress in a sea color (teal, purple, red, white), 1 per person (buy: thrift store, or own)
- Face paint in a matching accent color, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- Plastic trident prop, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Toy crab or red paper for a cardboard crab, 1 (make: cut from red paper, or buy: toy store)
- Shell necklace, 1 (buy: craft store, or make: string pasta shells)
- Scissors and tape, 1 set (own)

Steps:
1. Sketch the cheek detail on paper first. Face paint is hard to remove and redo once applied. Paint one small matching detail per person: scales on a cheek, a seaweed swirl, or an anchor.
2. Cut a red paper body, legs, and claws with the scissors and tape them to the smallest person's shirt. Or hand them the toy crab instead.
3. The sea king carries the plastic trident prop. Everyone else picks one accessory, like the shell necklace, and stands tall for the crew photo.
4. Optional pro finish: dab the accent face paint along the cheekbones through a fishnet stocking as a stencil. The scale stencil photographs like movie makeup.

Q: What if we cannot find sea-colored shirts?
A: Any solid tee works with the accessories doing the work. The trident plus the shell necklace plus one painted detail reads as mermaid crew on any color.

Q: How do you keep the crab on the shirt?
A: Tape it from inside the shirt with a big tape loop, or pin it. Do not tape it to bare skin; sweat loosens tape in an hour.

### Milk & Cookies

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/milk-cookies

White carton tunic for one, brown cookie with felt chips for the other.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- White t-shirt or tunic, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Brown t-shirt or tunic, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- White craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Brown craft felt, 2 sheets 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Black marker, 1 (own)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store, or raid the sewing kit)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy the felt, marker, and glue. Pull a white and a brown t-shirt from the closet.
2. Milk: cut the white felt into a carton-front rectangle about the size of a placemat. Write MILK across it in big block letters with the black marker.
3. Pin the carton front to the white t-shirt, pinning from inside the shirt so the pin backs face the fabric and never the skin.
4. Cookie: cut the biggest circle you can from the brown felt and pin it centered on the brown t-shirt.
5. Cut a dozen small chip shapes from the leftover brown felt and glue them onto the cookie circle. Uneven spacing looks more like a real cookie.
6. Safety: Check every pin from the inside before heading out, and keep glued felt flat so edges do not curl and catch.
7. Optional pro finish: the milk person carries a paper straw. One shared prop is what makes a pair read as a pair.

Q: How do you keep the felt pieces from flopping?
A: Pin each felt piece at 4 points, not 2. Felt pinned at the corners stays flat all night, and fabric glue on the chips keeps them from peeling.

Q: What if we have no brown felt?
A: A brown paper grocery bag cut into a circle works for one night. Glue paper chips on and pin the circle to the shirt.

### Moonwalking Pop Star

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/moonwalk-star

Red jacket, one glitter glove, and the lean everyone attempts.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red jacket, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Black pants, 1 (own)
- White glove, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Silver glitter glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Black fedora or hat, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- White socks, 1 pair (own)
- Black loafers or dress shoes, 1 pair (own)

Steps:
1. Cover one white glove in glitter glue and let it dry flat completely.
2. Wear the red jacket with black pants, white socks, and the fedora.
3. Put the glitter glove on one hand only. One glove, never two.
4. Practice the moonwalk and the toe-stand in socks on a smooth floor.
5. Safety: Practice the lean against a wall first, and never attempt it on a wet or crowded floor.
6. Optional pro finish: freeze mid-moonwalk when cameras appear. The frozen pose beats the dance.

Q: How do you keep the glitter on the glove?
A: Two thin coats of glitter glue, drying fully between coats, then a clear sealer. One thick coat sheds everywhere.

Q: What if we cannot find a red jacket?
A: A red hoodie with the hood down reads fine at party distance. The glove is the giveaway.

### Moth and Porch Light

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/moth-porch-light

One wears neutrals with cardboard wings; the other wears yellow and carries a lampshade.

Build time, effort: 40 min / Medium

Materials:
- Neutral shirt and pants in gray, brown, or tan, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Large cardboard box, 1 (own: cut two wing shapes from it)
- Brown and tan markers or paint, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Brown craft pipe cleaners, 2 (buy: craft store; brown yarn works too)
- Headband, 1 (own: from the drawer)
- Yellow t-shirt and yellow pants, 1 set (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Cone lampshade, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Tape, 1 roll, and scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Draw both wing ovals on the box first and have the moth hold their arms out to check the span.
2. Wings cut too small look like shoulder pads, and cardboard cut away cannot be put back.
3. Cut two large oval wing shapes from the large cardboard box with the scissors. Buy the brown craft pipe cleaners, brown and tan markers, and cone lampshade.
4. Draw eye spots and scalloped edges on the wings with the brown markers. Tape one wing to each arm of the neutral shirt and pants.
5. Bend the brown craft pipe cleaners into feathery antennae and tape them to the headband for the moth.
6. Put on the yellow t-shirt and yellow pants. Pop the cone lampshade over the head like a lampshade hat.
7. Stand next to the moth with arms out, buzzing.
8. Optional pro finish: curl the wing tips slightly forward and tape them so they cup inward. Real moth wings curve; flat cardboard reads as a sign.

Q: How do the wings stay on the arms?
A: Tape one wing to each sleeve of the neutral shirt with two strips of tape per wing. Tape on fabric holds for an evening; tape the wings to the sleeves, not to skin.

Q: What size lampshade for the porch light person?
A: One that fits over the head like a hat without covering the eyes, a medium table-lamp shade works. Check thrift stores.

### Mystery Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/mystery-crew

Assign the leader, the style icon, the brains, the goofball, and one very good dog.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Orange, purple, blue, and red t-shirts, 1 each (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Dog ears headband or a brown dog costume piece, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Fake magnifying glass, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: a paper circle taped to a stick)
- Headband or scarf in a matching color, 1 per person (own: from the drawer)
- Brown non-toxic face paint for the dog's nose, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Assign roles: orange leader, purple style icon, blue brains, red goofball, and the dog wears the ears.
2. Each person: put on their color's t-shirt and tie a matching headband or scarf.
3. The brains carries the fake magnifying glass. Paint a brown nose on the dog with the brown face paint.
4. Group the four humans in a line with the dog in front. All point at something suspicious for the classic pose.
5. Optional pro finish: write each person's role on a small paper name tag ('the brains', 'the leader'). The tags turn colored shirts into characters for anyone who does not know the reference.

Q: How do you assign the colors so people get the joke?
A: Orange leader, purple style icon, blue brains, red goofball, and the dog wears the ears. Assign before anyone dresses so no two people grab the same color.

Q: What if we only have four people, no dog?
A: Give the fourth person the dog ears over their colored shirt, the dog role is the most recognizable part, so it beats having a second of any human color.

### Mystery-Solving Teens

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/mystery-teens

Color-coded outfits, a toy magnifying glass, and one giant sandwich.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Solid-color tops in assigned colors, 1 per person (buy: at a thrift store, or own: from closets)
- Jeans or skirts, 1 per person (own)
- Toy magnifying glass, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Paper for the sandwich prop, 1 sheet (own)
- Dog plush or toy, 1 (own, or borrow one)
- Scarves or ascots in matching colors (own, or buy: thrift store)

Steps:
1. Assign each person a color: orange, blue, purple, green, red.
2. Everyone builds their outfit from their own closet in their assigned color.
3. One person carries the magnifying glass, one carries the giant paper sandwich.
4. Safety: The sandwich prop stays paper and light, and nothing gets swung in crowds.
5. Introduce yourselves in character when people ask. The names are the costume.
6. Optional pro finish: bring the dog plush and let one person carry it everywhere. The dog gets more photos than the teens.

Q: What if our group has only three people?
A: Pick any three colors. The color coding reads with three just as well as five.

Q: How do you make it obvious without name tags?
A: The magnifying glass, the sandwich, and the dog plush together tell the story. Props beat labels.

### Neon Demon Hunter

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/neon-demon-hunter

Streetwear with glowing sigils, a foam sword, and pop-idol hair and makeup.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 2 hrs drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black hoodie, black pants, chunky sneakers, 1 set (own)
- Neon fabric paint in 2 to 3 colors, 1 tube each (buy: craft store)
- Glow-in-the-dark temporary tattoos or neon eyeliner, 1 pack (buy: drugstore)
- Foam sword prop, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Hair gel or temporary neon hair spray, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Black leather-look jacket or vest, 1 (buy: thrift store, optional)

Steps:
1. Sketch the demon-slaying symbols on paper FIRST. Crooked symbols cannot be unpainted. Draw sharp neon symbols on the hoodie sleeves and pant legs with the fabric paint. Let dry 2 hours.
2. Style the hair up with hair gel, or mist it with the temporary neon hair spray. Apply the neon eyeliner or glow-in-the-dark temporary tattoos on the cheeks and arms.
3. Wear the black leather-look jacket over the hoodie and carry the foam sword prop. Keep the painted side facing out so the neon sigils show.
4. Optional pro finish: charge the neon paint under bright light before heading out, and add one glowing green 'scar' across the cheek with face paint. The scar is the backstory, everyone will ask about it.

Q: Does neon fabric paint actually glow?
A: It glows under blacklight and looks electric in daylight. Under normal indoor light it is just bright. For true night glow, add glow-in-the-dark tape accents.

Q: Toy sword or foam sword?
A: Foam. Toy plastic swords snap and leave sharp edges; foam swords survive all-night duels and venue security.
