### Ninja

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ninja

All black with a belt sash and a slit headband.

Build time, effort: 10 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- All-black outfit: t-shirt, pants, and a black beanie, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Black belt or sash, 1 (own: an old tie or scarf)
- Black headband or strip of black t-shirt, 1 strip about 3 inches wide (own: cut from an old shirt)
- Scissors, 1 pair, and tape, 1 roll (own: household tools)
- Black non-toxic face paint for a mask stripe, 1 tube (buy: drugstore, optional)

Steps:
1. Measure the strip around the forehead first and mark 3 inches wide BEFORE cutting, a strip cut too narrow digs in, and fabric cut away cannot be put back.
2. Cut the strip a little long from the old black t-shirt with the scissors; long can be trimmed, short cannot. Put on the black beanie.
3. Tie the black sash around the waist with the knot at the back, and tuck the ends in.
4. Safety: Keep the eyes and mouth uncovered, and wrap the black headband above the eyes.
5. Wrap the black headband around the forehead and tie it at the back, leaving the eyes clear.
6. Paint a thin black stripe across the bridge of the nose with the black face paint. Practice the silent sneaky walk.
7. Optional pro finish: tuck the headband ends in instead of letting them dangle. Clean lines read as trained ninja; loose ends read as pirate.
8. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: How do you wrap the headband so it is safe?
A: Wrap it above the eyes on the forehead and tie it at the back with a quick-release knot. Eyes and mouth stay completely uncovered, vision first, costume second.

Q: Do I need the face paint stripe?
A: No. The all-black outfit plus the forehead wrap already reads as ninja. The stripe is a nice touch for photos but skip it for kids who rub their faces.

### Numbered Players

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/numbered-players

Green tracksuits, numbered bibs, and a survival-game attitude.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Green sweatsuit per person, 1 each (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- White t-shirt per person, 1 each (own: from closet)
- Iron-on number patches or white paper numbers, 1 per person (buy: craft store)
- White sneakers, 1 pair per person (own: from closet)
- Dalgona candy or a round cookie per person, 1 each (buy: bakery, optional prop)
- Iron, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Lay the numbers on each shirt and have the wearers confirm their number BEFORE heating the iron, iron-on numbers cannot be repositioned once pressed.
2. Iron or tape one number onto the front of each white t-shirt and the matching number on the back.
3. Wear the white t-shirt under the green sweatsuit jacket with the number showing, plus the white sneakers.
4. Hand each player a dalgona candy as the prop. Line up in number order for the photo.
5. Safety: If using an iron, have an adult do the pressing. Keep numbers readable and identical front and back.
6. Optional pro finish: draw a thin triangle border around each number with a black fabric marker. The border is what makes the number read as a player badge instead of a sticker.

Q: Iron-on numbers or taped paper numbers?
A: Iron-on for teens and adults who will keep the shirt; taped paper numbers for kids or borrowed shirts. Tape survives one evening fine and peels off clean.

Q: What if we cannot find green sweatsuits?
A: Any green top and pants work, the white numbered t-shirt over green is the whole read. The sweatsuit is a nice-to-have, not the costume.

### Office Couple

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/office-couple

White shirts, name tags, and a teapot. The office's finest.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- White button-down shirts, 2 (own: from closet)
- Name tags, 2 (buy: office supply store, or make: index cards with safety pins)
- Toy teapot or a small real teapot, 1 (own: from the kitchen)
- Black pants or skirts, 2 (own: from closet)
- Marker for writing names, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Buy name tags, or make them from index cards and safety pins. Pull the white button-down shirts and black pants or skirts from the closet.
2. Write joke job titles on the name tags with the marker and pin them on the white button-down shirts.
3. One person carries the toy teapot proudly all evening. The other carries a clipboard or a stack of papers.
4. Tuck the white button-down shirts in and straighten each other's collars. Introduce yourselves by your fake titles to everyone you meet.
5. Optional pro finish: write the fake titles in a dead-serious font, like 'Regional Teapot Manager'. The comedy is in how official the name tag looks.

Q: What are good joke job titles?
A: Pick titles that match the props: 'Director of Teapot Operations' for the teapot carrier, 'VP of Paperwork' for the clipboard holder. Specific beats random.

Q: Is a real teapot okay to carry around?
A: A small empty one is fine, but a toy or plastic teapot is better, real ceramic breaks if set down hard, and a full teapot is heavy by hour two.

### Party Pinata

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/party-pinata

A cardboard box wrapped in rainbow fringe, with real candy inside.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 30 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- Cardboard box, 1 large (make: from a shipping box)
- Crepe paper in rainbow colors, 6 rolls (buy: dollar store)
- Wrapped candy, 2 bags (buy: grocery store)
- String for hanging strips, 1 roll (own)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut fringe strips from the crepe paper and glue them in overlapping rows over the whole box.
2. Cut arm and head holes in the box, with the opening at the bottom for candy.
3. Fill the box with wrapped candy before sealing the bottom flap loosely.
4. Safety: Keep the head hole generous so vision and breathing stay easy, and use only wrapped candy.
5. Hand out candy from inside the costume all night. The giving is the costume.
6. Optional pro finish: let kids pull one candy each from the bottom flap. You become the party game.

Q: How do you keep the fringe from tearing?
A: Glue each fringe row at the top edge only, overlapping downward. Rows glued flat across tear when you move.

Q: Will the box survive the whole party?
A: Double-wall cardboard survives a night. Single-ply boxes crush by midnight.

### Peanut Butter & Jelly

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pbj

One in brown with a PB label, one in purple with a J label.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Brown t-shirt, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Purple t-shirt, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- White poster board, 2 sheets (buy: dollar store)
- Markers, 1 set (own: household)
- Scissors, 1 pair, and tape or string, 1 roll or spool (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Draw the bread shape on the poster board first and hold it against the t-shirt to check the size.
2. Bread cut too small looks like a badge, and poster board cut away cannot be put back.
3. Cut two big sandwich-bread shapes from the white poster board with the scissors, cutting generous and trimming after the fitting. Buy the brown t-shirt, purple t-shirt, and white poster board if needed.
4. Write 'PB' in big letters on one bread shape and 'J' on the other with the markers.
5. Tape or string one bread sign to the front of the brown t-shirt. Tape or string the other to the front of the purple t-shirt.
6. Stand pressed together all evening, bread sides out. The brown-shirt person is the peanut butter and the purple-shirt person is the jelly.
7. Optional pro finish: draw a wavy crust edge around each bread shape with a tan marker. The crust line is what makes it read as bread instead of a white sign.

Q: Which side is peanut butter and which is jelly?
A: Brown shirt is peanut butter, purple shirt is jelly. Label the bread signs 'PB' and 'J' big enough to read from ten feet away so nobody has to ask.

Q: How do you wear the bread signs?
A: Tape or string one bread sign to the front of each t-shirt like a sandwich board front panel. Two attachment points at the top corners keep it from spinning.

### Peas in a Pod

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/peas-pod

Green shirts in a row under one long felt pod sash.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Green t-shirts, 1 per person for 3 to 5 people (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Green felt, 1 yard (buy: craft store; green fabric works too)
- Green fabric paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Hot glue gun or fabric glue, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Lay the group out and chalk the pod outline on the felt against their actual lineup BEFORE cutting, a pod cut too short strands a pea outside, and felt cut away cannot be put back.
2. Cut the green felt into one long pod shape with the scissors, about 6 feet long, with a pointed top, cutting long and trimming later.
3. Buy the green felt, green fabric paint, and hot glue gun.
4. Paint darker green stripes and a center seam line down the pod with the green fabric paint. Let the paint dry for 1 hour.
5. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue gun, and keep fingers away from the nozzle.
6. Glue the pod to the front of the green t-shirts so it stretches across all of them. Space the wearers evenly.
7. Paint a small green circle on each person's cheek with the green face paint. Line everyone up in height order under the pod and walk together in a row.
8. Optional pro finish: paint each person's name on the pod next to their spot. Named peas turn a group costume into a keepsake photo.

Q: How many people make a good pea pod?
A: Three to five. Two looks thin, six stretches the felt so far the pod sags. Three peas in a pod is the classic for a reason.

Q: How do the peas stay lined up while walking?
A: Space the wearers evenly and walk in a row at the same pace, practice once before going out. The pod is one piece, so if one person rushes, the whole pod bunches.

---

### Penguin Huddle

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/penguin-huddle

Black shirts, felt bellies, beak headbands. Waddle together.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black long-sleeve shirts, 1 per person (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- White felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person (buy: craft store; white paper works too)
- Orange felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches per person (buy: craft store; orange paper works too)
- Headbands, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Cut one paper belly template first and check it against a shirt, a belly cut too small looks like a bib, and felt cut away cannot be put back.
2. Then cut an oval white belly from the white felt with the scissors for each person. Buy the white felt, orange felt, headbands, and fabric glue.
3. Cut a small orange triangle beak from the orange felt for each headband. Glue one beak to the front of each headband with the fabric glue.
4. Glue the white bellies to the front of the black long-sleeve shirts. Let the fabric glue dry for 30 minutes.
5. Each person: put on the black long-sleeve shirt and the headband with the beak. Tuck hands into the sleeves as flippers and waddle shoulder to shoulder in the huddle.
6. Optional pro finish: cut two small orange felt feet shapes and tape them over the toes of dark shoes. Feet are the detail people notice in full-body photos.

Q: How big should the white belly be?
A: An oval that covers the chest from collarbone to waistband. Too small reads as a badge; chest-size reads as a penguin belly instantly.

Q: How do you keep the beak on the headband?
A: Glue one orange triangle beak to the front of each headband with fabric glue and let it dry flat for 30 minutes. Glue beats tape here, tape peels off headbands by the second hour.

### Pickle

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pickle

Green tunic, bumpy texture, smug grin.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Green tunic or oversized green t-shirt, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Green bubble wrap or green pom-poms, about 20 bumps (buy: craft store, or make: twist bits of green fabric)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Green non-toxic face paint, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)

Steps:
1. Lay out all the bumps on the tunic DRY first and step back to check the pattern is even, once fabric glue sets, bumps cannot be moved.
2. Space them in a loose grid so no bare patches show. Glue the bumps all over the front and back of the tunic for the bumpy pickle texture.
3. Let the fabric glue dry flat for 30 minutes.
4. Paint the face, then draw on a smug grin with one raised eyebrow.
5. Wear the tunic over regular clothes and stand tall.
6. Optional pro finish: add a slightly darker green felt band at the top and bottom of the tunic. The bands frame the bumps and make it read as a whole pickle instead of a bumpy shirt.

Q: Bubble wrap or pom-poms for the bumps?
A: Pom-poms look better and stay put; bubble wrap pops when people hug you and goes flat by midnight. If you use bubble wrap, pop it yourself first for a dimpled texture that lasts.

Q: How much of the face should be green?
A: Full face in a light layer, keeping it clear of the eyes. A half-green face reads as sick; a full light-green face with a smug grin reads as pickle.

### Pirate Captain

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pirate-captain

Striped shirt, cardboard captain hat, and a treasure map you drew yourself.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Striped shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Dark pants, 1 (own)
- Cardboard for the hat, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Black eye patch, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: from felt and elastic)
- Toy sword or cardboard cutlass, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: from cardboard)
- Brown paper for the treasure map, 1 sheet (own)
- Black marker, 1 (own)
- Gold plastic coins, 1 bag (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut the captain hat from cardboard: a wide crescent with the front folded up, and tape the seam.
2. Draw the treasure map on the brown paper with the black marker, with an X and a dotted route.
3. Wear the striped shirt with the pants, the eye patch, and the hat.
4. Safety: Use a cardboard or foam sword, never a real blade, and keep the map rolled when walking in crowds.
5. Hand out gold coins to kids you meet. A pirate who shares treasure is remembered.
6. Optional pro finish: learn one pirate phrase and commit to it all night. The voice is half the costume.

Q: How do you keep the cardboard hat on?
A: Cut the hat slightly small and add an elastic chin strap. A hat that fits snug beats one that fits pretty.

Q: Can a whole group do this together?
A: Yes: one captain hat for the leader, bandanas for the crew, same striped shirts. The crew reads instantly.

### Pixel Ghost

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pixel-ghost

A white sheet cut in chunky pixel squares with felt eyes.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- White bedsheet or white fabric, 1 twin-size (buy: thrift store)
- Black felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; black paper works too)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)
- Marker and ruler, 1 each (own: household)

Steps:
1. Fold the sheet in half and chalk the zigzag line first, holding it against the wearer to check the length.
2. A hem cut too short cannot be fixed, and this is the bottom edge of the whole costume.
3. Cut the bottom edge into chunky square zigzags with the scissors, about 4 inches per square, cutting long and trimming later. Buy the white bedsheet and the black felt.
4. Draw two square eyes and a square mouth on the black felt with the marker and ruler. Cut them out.
5. Glue the felt eyes and mouth onto the top third of the white bedsheet. Let the fabric glue dry for 30 minutes.
6. Safety: Keep the eye area open so vision stays clear.
7. Wear dark clothes underneath and drape the white bedsheet over the head with the eyes lined up. Cut two small arm slits if reaching through is hard.
8. Optional pro finish: cut two small arm slits at the sides. Reaching through slits instead of lifting the whole sheet keeps the ghost shape intact all night.

Q: How do you keep the pixel edges crisp?
A: Use the ruler and marker to draw the zigzag grid before cutting, and cut on the lines. Freehand zigzags wobble; measured squares read as pixels.

Q: How does the wearer see?
A: Wear dark clothes underneath, drape the sheet over the head, and leave the face area open under the felt eyes, the eyes are decoration on the sheet, not eye holes. Vision stays fully clear.

### Pizza Slice

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pizza-slice

A big cardboard triangle, painted golden with felt pepperoni.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Large cardboard box, 1 (make: cut a big triangle, about 3 feet tall)
- Yellow and orange acrylic paint, 1 bottle each (buy: craft store)
- Red felt, 1 sheet (buy: craft store; red paper works too)
- Brown felt scraps for crust, or 1 brown paper bag (buy: craft store)
- Paintbrush, scissors, tape, 1 set (own)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Paint the whole triangle a golden yellow-orange with the paintbrush and let it dry 1 hour.
2. Arrange the pepperoni on the triangle DRY first. Pepperoni clusters in the middle if you glue as you go.
3. Cut red felt circles and glue them spread out, then add the brown crust strip along the wide end.
4. Tape two string loops to the back so it wears like a sandwich board. Keep the crust at the top and the point at the bottom.
5. Optional pro finish: add green felt 'peppers' and white felt 'cheese drips' along the top edge. Toppings are what separate a pizza slice from a yellow triangle.

Q: How do you make it read as pizza, not just yellow?
A: The crust strip along the bottom is the key, a yellow shirt with pepperoni is ambiguous, with a crust it is pizza. Add the crust.

Q: Slice or whole pizza for a group?
A: One slice each, standing in a circle, makes a whole pizza when you huddle. The group photo where you form the pizza is the whole point.

### Plague Doctor

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/plague-doctor

Long coat, wide hat, beaked mask.

Build time, effort: 60 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Long black coat or black robe, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Wide-brim black hat, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Black half mask or sunglasses, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Cardboard or craft foam for the beak, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; stiff paper works too)
- Black gloves, 1 pair (buy: dollar store)
- Hot glue gun, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Black spray paint or black markers, 1 can or set (buy: craft store)

Steps:
1. Cut a paper beak template first and hold it against the mask to check the curve and length.
2. A beak cut too long looks silly and one cut too short looks stubby, and neither can be fixed after cutting.
3. Cut a long curved beak shape from the cardboard or craft foam with the scissors. Buy the coat, hat, mask, gloves, hot glue gun, and beak materials.
4. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot glue gun, and keep fingers away from the nozzle.
5. Paint the beak black with the black spray paint and let it dry. Hot-glue the beak to the front of the black half mask so it juts out.
6. Safety: Fit the black half mask so the eyes are fully open. Never wear a mask that blocks peripheral vision.
7. Cut round eye holes in the black half mask and fit it so the eyes are fully open.
8. Wear the long black coat, wide-brim black hat, black gloves, and the beaked mask together. Carry a wooden staff or walking stick for the full effect.
9. Optional pro finish: paint the finished beak with a second light coat and let it dry fully. One thin coat looks gray in flash photos; two coats read as true black.
10. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: How do you attach the beak to the mask?
A: Hot-glue the beak to the front of the black half mask so it juts forward, with an adult handling the glue gun. Test the fit before gluing, the mask must sit so the eyes are fully open.

Q: Is the mask safe to wear while walking around?
A: Only if the eyes are fully open with clear peripheral vision. Never wear a mask that blocks side vision near stairs, streets, or crowds, take it off to walk between houses.

### Plastic Dream Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/plastic-dream-crew

Head-to-toe pink outfits with plastic accessories for the dream crew.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- All-pink outfit per person: dress, suit, or sweatsuit, 1 set each (buy: a set at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Pink sunglasses, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Plastic play accessories: phone, tiara, handbag, 1 per person (buy: a set at a dollar store, or own: from the toy box)
- Pink feather boa, 1 to share (buy: dollar store, optional)
- Blonde wig, 1 per person (buy: costume aisle, optional)

Steps:
1. Pull an all-pink outfit per person from the closet. Buy the pink sunglasses and feather boa.
2. Everyone wears pink head to toe with the pink sunglasses. Add the tiara, handbag, or toy phone.
3. Drape the feather boa over whoever is feeling the most plastic today.
4. Strike the wave-and-smile pose. Everything is pink, and that is the whole point.
5. Optional pro finish: give everyone the same accessory, matching sunglasses or matching purses. Uniform accessories are what turn pink outfits into a crew.
6. Optional pro finish: try the wig on for 20 minutes before the party. Itchy wigs get ripped off by nine.

Q: Do you need the wigs?
A: No, matching pink outfits plus matching accessories carry it. Wigs help but the uniformity is the costume, not the hair.

Q: How do you keep it from looking like just pink clothes?
A: Commit to the bit: wave like a doll, pose like a doll, talk like everything is fantastic. The performance is the costume.

### Player One & Two

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/player-one-two

Matching tees with 1 and 2, toy controllers in hand, ready for co-op.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Matching t-shirts, 2, any color (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Iron-on letters or fabric markers, spelling 1 and 2 (buy: craft store)
- Toy game controllers, 2 (buy: toy store, or make: draw one on cardboard)
- Iron, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Put a big '1' on the front and back of one t-shirt with the iron-on letters. Put a big '2' on the front and back of the other t-shirt.
2. Safety: Let an adult handle the hot iron on a hard surface.
3. Pin or tape the letters to the shirts and check the size and position in a mirror BEFORE heating the iron, ironed letters cannot be repositioned.
4. Iron the letters onto the t-shirts on a hard surface with an adult handling the iron, or draw them with the fabric markers.
5. Each player: wear their numbered t-shirt and carry a toy game controller.
6. Walk in together, controllers up, and argue good-naturedly all evening about who is really player one.
7. Optional pro finish: add a small 'INSERT COIN' label under each number with a fabric marker. It is the detail that gets the laugh from anyone over thirty.

Q: No iron, what is the best alternative?
A: Fabric markers, drawn big. Iron-on looks cleaner but marker numbers survive the night fine, and you can skip the whole adult-with-a-hot-iron step.

Q: How big should the numbers be?
A: Chest-filling: about 8 inches tall on an adult shirt, 5 inches on a kid shirt. Numbers smaller than that disappear in group photos.

### Plug and Socket

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/plug-socket

Cardboard plug and outlet worn front and back.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Cardboard box, 1 large (own: cut two flat panels, one per person)
- Gray and white acrylic paint, 1 small bottle each (buy: craft store)
- Black markers, 1 set (own: household)
- Craft foam, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store; cardboard works too)
- Tape, 1 roll, and string, 1 spool, for wearing (own: household tools)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: household tools)

Steps:
1. Mark the panel size against each wearer BEFORE cutting, a panel cut too small looks like a badge and one cut too big bangs knees, and cardboard cut away cannot be put back.
2. Cut two cardboard panels from the large box with the scissors, each about 2 feet square, one per person, cutting generous and trimming later. Buy the gray and white acrylic paint and the craft foam.
3. Make the plug: paint one panel gray. Draw two prongs on the craft foam, cut them out, and tape them sticking up from the top edge.
4. Make the socket: paint the other panel white. Draw two dark slots and a round outlet face with the black markers.
5. Fix the string to the back corners of each panel with tape so they hang like sandwich boards. The plug person stands next to the socket person.
6. Optional pro finish: paint a small lightning bolt between the two panels' meeting edges. The bolt sells the 'about to connect' joke in photos.

Q: How do the panels stay on?
A: Fix string to the back corners of each panel with tape so they hang like sandwich boards, front and back. Two strings per panel, not one, so nothing spins around.

Q: Cardboard prongs or foam prongs for the plug?
A: Craft foam, it is light, it will not poke anyone, and it tapes on cleanly. Cardboard prongs snap off by the second hour.

### Plumber Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/plumber-duo

Overalls, red and green caps and shirts, drawn mustaches.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Blue overalls, 2 (buy: thrift store)
- Red t-shirt and green t-shirt, 1 each (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Red cap and green cap, 1 each (buy: dollar store)
- Brown non-toxic face paint for mustaches, 1 tube (buy: drugstore)
- White circle stickers or white paper, 2 about 2 inches across (buy: dollar store)
- Marker, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Write a big 'M' on one white circle and an 'L' on the other with the marker. Stick or tape them to the front of the red cap and green cap.
2. Each brother: wear the blue overalls over their colored t-shirt and cap. Paint on a mustache with the brown face paint.
3. The red brother gets a big bushy one, and the green brother gets a thinner one.
4. Roll the overall cuffs once and strike the jump pose with a fist in the air. Talk about fixing pipes all night.
5. Optional pro finish: roll the overall cuffs once and scuff the knees with a little brown face paint. Work-worn overalls read as plumbers; crisp new ones read as a uniform costume.

Q: How do you tell the two plumbers apart?
A: Red shirt and cap with an 'M' circle for the older brother, green with an 'L' for the younger. The cap letters are the tell, get them on straight and centered.

Q: How do you paint a mustache that lasts?
A: Brown face paint with a fingertip, two coats, keeping it above the lip line. It fades when eating, so bring the tube for a touch-up halfway through the night.

### Pocket Plush Monster

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pocket-plush

A fuzzy one-piece, giant ears, a stitched smile, and an oversized collector tag.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Fuzzy one-piece pajamas or sweatsuit, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Felt ears: two big felt circles, about 4 inches across (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Black and white felt for eyes and smile, 1 small sheet each (buy: craft store; paper works too)
- Large shipping tag or big index card, 1 (buy: office supply store)
- Marker, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Cut the eyes and smile from paper first and lay them on the pajama chest to check the size and spacing, glued felt cannot be repositioned.
2. Then cut two white felt eyes and a stitched-look smile from the black felt, and glue them to the chest of the fuzzy pajamas with the fabric glue.
3. Write a collector number like 'No. 001' on the large shipping tag with the marker. Tie the tag to the wrist or waistband with string.
4. Wear the fuzzy one-piece pajamas with the felt ears and large shipping tag showing. The smile goes on the chest like a plush's embroidered face.
5. Optional pro finish: stitch the smile with dashed lines using a white fabric marker instead of a solid line. Dashed stitches read as plush embroidery; a solid line reads as a drawing.

Q: How do the ears stay on the hood?
A: Fabric glue with the hood laid flat, left to dry for 30 minutes before wearing. For a same-night build, safety-pin them from inside the hood instead, pins hold immediately.

Q: What do you write on the shipping tag?
A: A collector number like 'No. 001' plus the plush name. The tag is the joke, so make it look official: big number, neat letters.

### Pop Star

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/pop-star

A sparkly jacket, a toy microphone, and the biggest hair in the room.

Build time, effort: 15 min / Easy

Materials:
- Sparkly or sequin jacket, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Toy microphone, 1 (buy: toy store or dollar store)
- Hair teasing comb, 1 (own, or buy: drugstore)
- Sunglasses, 1 pair (own, or buy: dollar store)
- Dark jeans and a dark top, 1 set (own)

Steps:
1. Tease the hair big with the comb.
2. Safety: Go easy teasing near the scalp; no pulling hard.
3. Wear the sparkly jacket over the dark jeans and top.
4. Put on the sunglasses.
5. Carry the toy microphone everywhere and take requests.
6. Optional pro finish: learn one 8-count of choreography and do it on request all night. A pop star who performs is unforgettable; one who just stands there is overdressed.

Q: Which pop star should I pick?
A: Whoever's outfit you can build from your closet, the hair and the attitude matter more than the exact outfit. Commit to one era, not a mashup.

Q: How do you get big pop-star hair?
A: Backcomb the crown, spray it, and let the ends stay smooth. Volume on top, smooth below, that is the silhouette.

### Popcorn Bucket

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/popcorn-bucket

A striped cardboard-box body with balloon popcorn on top.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Cardboard box, 1 medium (make: tall enough to cover the torso)
- Red and white striped wrapping paper or paint, 1 roll (buy: dollar store or craft store)
- Yellow or white balloons, 8 to 10 (buy: dollar store)
- Tape, string, scissors, 1 set (own)
- Red marker for the label, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Cut the head and arm holes SMALL first and test the fit. Holes cut too big cannot be shrunk. Tape the inside edges of the holes so the cardboard does not scratch.
2. Blow up the yellow or white balloons and tie them in a cluster. Tie the cluster to a string ring that sits on top of the box like overflowing popcorn.
3. Step into the box and pull the string straps over the shoulders. Carry the popcorn crown carefully through doorways.
4. Optional pro finish: glue a few 'popcorn' pieces to the rim as if overflowing. Overflowing reads as fresh and generous; a flat top reads as empty.

Q: Balloons or tissue paper for the popcorn?
A: Tissue paper, crumpled white tissue looks like popcorn and weighs nothing. Balloons pop and squeak all night.

Q: How do you wear the bucket?

### Prince & Princess

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/prince-princess

A crown and cape, a thrifted gown and tiara.

Build time, effort: 10 min / Easy

Materials:
- Gold paper crown or plastic crown, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: cut one from gold poster board)
- Cape or long piece of fabric, 1 about 3 feet long (buy: thrift store)
- Thrifted gown or long dress, 1 (buy: thrift store)
- Tiara, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Toy scepter or wand, 1 (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. The prince: wear the gold paper crown and cape over dark clothes, and carry the toy scepter.
2. The princess: wear the thrifted gown and tiara, and add the spare wand if there is one.
3. Walk in with royal posture, wave slowly with a bent wrist, and address everyone as 'my good subject'.
4. Optional pro finish: give the prince a sash of torn fabric across the chest. A sash plus a crown reads as royalty; a crown alone reads as a party hat.

Q: How do you keep a paper crown on all night?
A: Size it snug and tape the join on the inside, then add two bobby pins through the crown into the hair. Paper crowns fail at the join, so reinforce the join before anything else.

Q: What should the prince wear under the cape?

Pinstripe suit and pumpkin mask for one, patchwork dress and yarn hair for the other.

### Rain Cloud and Rainbow

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/rain-cloud-rainbow

One wears gray with cotton clouds and paper raindrops; the other wears rainbow stripes.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Gray t-shirt or sweatshirt, 1 (buy: thrift store, or own: from closet)
- White cotton balls or polyester stuffing, 1 bag (buy: dollar store or craft store)
- Blue paper raindrops, about 15 (own: cut from blue construction paper)
- String, 1 spool, and tape, 1 roll (own: household tools)
- Fabric glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Rainbow-striped shirt, 1, or a white shirt, 1, plus rainbow fabric markers, 1 set (buy: thrift store or craft store)
- Blue non-toxic face paint for one rain streak, 1 tube (buy: drugstore, optional)

Steps:
1. Arrange the cotton balls on the shirt DRY first and step back to check the cloud coverage, once fabric glue sets, cotton balls cannot be moved.
2. Plan for full coverage with no gray showing through the middle. Then glue the cotton balls in clumps across the gray t-shirt to make clouds.
3. Fix the blue paper raindrops to short pieces of string with tape. Hang the strings from the bottom edge of the gray t-shirt so they dangle.
4. The rainbow person: wear the rainbow-striped shirt, or draw rainbow arcs across a white shirt with the rainbow fabric markers.
5. Stand side by side: the cloud holds arms out wide. The rainbow stands just behind, peeking out after the 'storm'.
6. Add one blue rain streak on a cheek with the blue face paint if you like.
7. Optional pro finish: hang the raindrops at staggered lengths, not all even. Uneven drops look like real rain; a straight row looks like a mobile.

Q: How many cotton balls for a full cloud shirt?
A: Most of a dollar-store bag, plan on 40 to 60 for an adult shirt, 25 to 35 for a kid. Skimpy clouds show gray through the middle and read as lint, not weather.

Q: How do the raindrops stay hanging?
A: Fix each blue paper raindrop to a short piece of string with tape, then tape the strings along the bottom edge of the shirt. Short strings, about 4 inches, tangle less than long ones.

### Ramen Bowl

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/ramen-bowl

Cardboard bowl rim, noodle-yarn hair, a foam egg on top.

Build time, effort: 50 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Large cardboard circle, about 2 feet wide (make: cut from a big box)
- White and red acrylic paint, 2 small bottles (buy: craft store)
- Yellow yarn, 1 skein (buy: craft store; yellow string works too)
- White craft foam or 1 foam ball (buy: craft store; white paper works too)
- Chopsticks, 1 pair (own: kitchen drawer)
- Tape and string, 1 roll and about 2 feet (own: household)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Test the bowl rim size before cutting: hold the cardboard up and mark where it should sit as a hat.
2. Cut the cardboard circle into a wide bowl rim shape with the scissors, cutting a little larger than you think since you can trim it down but cannot add cardboard back.
3. Paint it white with a red stripe and let it dry fully, about 1 hour.
4. Make the noodles: cut dozens of 12-inch yellow yarn strands. Fasten them in a tangled layer across the top of the dry bowl rim with the tape.
5. Cut the white craft foam into a half egg shape and paint a yellow yolk dot on it.
6. Let it dry, then tape the egg on top of the noodles and stick the chopsticks in at an angle.
7. Wear the bowl rim like a hat with string under the chin, noodles and egg on top. Slurp loudly for effect.
8. Optional pro finish: glue two real wooden chopsticks crossed at the top of the noodles, and tape a paper logo circle to the bowl rim so it reads as a branded ramen bowl.

Q: How do you wear the bowl so it does not fall off?
A: Wear the bowl rim like a hat with string tied under the chin, noodles and egg on top. Keep the string snug but loose enough to slip a finger under.

Q: What can you use instead of yellow yarn for the noodles?
A: Yellow string, shredded yellow paper, or thin strips of a yellow plastic bag all read as noodles. Tape them in a tangled layer so they look piled, not combed.

### Raptor Barista

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/raptor-barista

Green hoodie with a dino snout hood, tiny T. rex arms strapped on, and a coffee cup you can barely hold.

- Green hoodie, 1 (buy: clothing store, or use your own)

Q: How do the tiny arms stay on?

Q: What if I cannot find toy dinosaur arms?

### Raptor & Ranger

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/raptor-ranger

One khaki ranger, one green dino hood. The ranger holds the leash.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Khaki shirt and hat for the ranger, 1 set (own: from closet, or buy at a thrift store)
- Green hoodie or green t-shirt for the raptor, 1 (own: from closet)
- Green felt sheet, 9x12 inches, 1 (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Rope, 3 feet, or 1 toy dog leash (buy: pet aisle)
- Face paint, green and black, 1 set (buy: costume aisle or craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair, and tape, 1 roll (own: household)

Steps:
1. Decide who is the ranger and who is the raptor, then lay out both outfits. Buy the 3 ft rope or toy dog leash and the face paint if you do not have them.
2. Safety: Cut the green felt sheet slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
3. Draw the tail shape on the felt first and hold it up to the raptor's back to check the length before cutting, since a too-short tail cannot be lengthened.
4. Then cut one long triangle from the green felt sheet for the tail. Tape it to the back of the raptor's green shirt so it hangs behind them.
5. The ranger wears the khaki shirt and hat with the toy dog leash in hand. The raptor wears the green shirt with the tail attached.
6. Safety: Use non-toxic kids face paint, and skip any mask so the raptor can see clearly.
7. Paint the raptor's snout: use the green face paint to draw a snout and two black dots for nostrils. Then the ranger holds the toy dog leash out toward the raptor for photos.
8. Optional pro finish: tie the rope as a belt around the ranger's waist and clip a toy walkie-talkie to it for the field-guide look.

Q: How long should the leash be?
A: Keep the leash short, about 2 to 3 feet, so the toy dinosaur does not drag on the ground. Tie the wrist end in a loop so it cannot tighten.

Q: What face paint is safe for kids?
A: Use non-toxic kids face paint and skip any mask so the raptor can see clearly. Keep paint off the lips and wash it off the same night.

### Referee

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/referee

A striped shirt, a whistle, and a yellow penalty flag.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Plain black t-shirt or long-sleeve shirt, 1 (own: from closet)
- Black pants or shorts, 1 pair (own: from closet)
- White athletic tape, 1 roll (buy: sporting goods or pharmacy)
- Plastic whistle, 1 (buy: dollar store or sporting goods)
- Yellow fabric square, 6x6 inches (own: cut from an old cloth or napkin)

Steps:
1. Tear horizontal strips of the white athletic tape across the front and back of the black shirt. Space them about 2 inches apart and press firmly so they stay.
2. Fold the yellow fabric square in half and tie it in a knot around the whistle lanyard. Or tape it to the whistle so it waves when you blow the whistle.
3. Wear the black outfit with the striped shirt and put the whistle around your neck. Tuck the yellow flag in a pocket.
4. Optional pro finish: add a black wristband on one wrist and carry the yellow flag tucked in a back pocket, hidden until the call.

Q: Will the athletic tape stay on the shirt all night?
A: Press each strip firmly onto a clean, dry shirt and the tape holds for the evening. It peels off after, though it can pull lint on fuzzy fabrics, so test a hidden spot first.

Q: What can I use instead of a real whistle?
A: A toy whistle from a party favor pack works, or just mime blowing it. Skip loud metal whistles around small kids.

### Rescue Pup Team

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/rescue-pups

Color-coded pup vests and felt ears for the whole preschool crew.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

### Cardboard Robot Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/robot-crew

Boxy robots built from cardboard boxes, foil, and bottle-cap buttons.

Build time, effort: 45 min / Medium

Materials:
- Medium cardboard box per person, 1 each (make: from home or moving boxes)
- Small cardboard box per person for the head, 1 each (make: from cereal or shoe boxes)
- Aluminum foil, 1 large roll (buy: grocery store)
- Plastic bottle caps, about 20 total (own)
- Duct tape, 1 roll (buy: hardware store)
- Black permanent marker, 1 (own)
- Elastic string or yarn, 6 feet (buy: craft store)
- Glow sticks, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Cut the eye holes BIG. You can cover extra space with foil, but you cannot add cardboard back. Cut the boxes slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
2. Cut head and arm holes in each medium cardboard box so they slide over the torso. Cut eye holes in the small cardboard boxes for heads.
3. Wrap every box in aluminum foil, taping the foil down with duct tape.
4. Draw dials and gauges on the chest with the black permanent marker. Tape the plastic bottle caps next to the dials as buttons.
5. Wrap leftover aluminum foil around each arm from wrist to shoulder and tape the ends with duct tape. Or cut the armholes in the torso box big enough to slide bare arms through.
6. Each person slides into a torso box and holds or ties the small cardboard box on their head.
7. Tie the elastic string under the chin to keep the head box on. Crack a glow stick and tape it to the chest as a power light.
8. Optional pro finish: give each robot a name badge ('UNIT 7', 'BEEP BOOP'). Named robots get talked to; unnamed robots get looked at. The badge is the personality.

Q: How do you keep a robot crew looking like a crew?
A: Same silver, same box proportions, different button layouts. Uniform base plus unique details, that is the crew formula.

Q: What is the best robot crew move?
A: Move in sync, stop, turn heads together, beep in unison. Synchronized robots are ten times funnier than individual robots.

---

### Robot Ranger

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/robot-ranger

Silver boxes, dryer-vent arms, and sticker dials.

Build time, effort: 60 min / Medium

Materials:
- Medium cardboard box for the torso, 1 (own: from home)
- Aluminum foil, 1 roll (buy: grocery store)
- Flexible aluminum dryer vent hose, 1 section about 3 feet (buy: hardware store)
- Sticker dots or round stickers, 1 sheet (buy: craft store; punched paper circles work too)
- Duct tape, 1 roll (buy: hardware store)
- Blue or gray sweatsuit to wear underneath, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Black marker, 1 (own: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Safety: Cut the cardboard box slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors. The dryer vent hose has sharp wire edges, so cut carefully and tape the ends right away.
2. Before cutting, wear the box over your head and trace circles for the head and arm holes a little bigger than you need.
3. Cut the holes SMALLER than traced first, since you can widen them but cannot shrink them. Then wrap the box in aluminum foil like a gift, taping the foil flat.
4. Draw two round gauges on the foil chest with the black marker. Stick the sticker dots on as dial needles and button lights.
5. Hold the hose pieces against your arms to measure the length before cutting, and cut longer than you need since cut hose cannot be repaired.
6. The dryer vent hose has sharp wire edges, so tape the ends right away so the wire ribs stay put.
7. Tape the top of each piece to the shoulder holes of the box so arms slide inside.
8. Dress in the blue or gray sweatsuit and slide the foil-wrapped cardboard box over the head and arms. Press the sticker dials on last so they sit on the chest.
9. Optional pro finish: add a big red sticker dot as an emergency button on the chest, and draw a small speaker grille under it with the black marker.

Q: How do you handle the sharp edges on the vent hose?
A: Cut carefully and tape both ends immediately so the wire ribs stay put. Wear the sweatsuit underneath so no foil or wire touches bare skin.

Q: Can the kid see and breathe inside the box?
A: Cut the head hole generous and keep the box loose on the shoulders. Never tape the box to the head, and take it off indoors in crowds.

### Safari Photographer

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/safari-photographer

Khaki vest, toy camera and binoculars, plus a stuffed lion cub under one arm.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Khaki vest with pockets, 1 (buy: thrift store, or wear a tan button-down from closet)
- Khaki pants or shorts, 1 pair (own: from closet)
- Toy camera, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: draw a camera on cardboard and tape a strap)
- Toy binoculars, 1 (buy: dollar store; two paper towel rolls taped together work too)
- Stuffed lion or lion cub toy, 1 (buy: thrift store or toy aisle)
- Safari hat, 1 (buy: costume aisle, or wear any wide-brim hat from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair; tape, 1 roll; marker, 1 (own: household)

Steps:
1. Buy or gather the toy camera, toy binoculars, stuffed lion or lion cub toy, and safari hat.
2. Pull the khaki pants and khaki vest from the closet.
3. Safety: Cut the cardboard slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Sketch the camera shape on the cardboard first and cut one size up, then trim down after a test fitting.
5. To make the camera: cut a camera shape from cardboard and draw a lens with a marker. Tape a ribbon or belt through it as a strap.
6. Dress in the khaki pants, khaki vest, and safari hat. Hang the toy camera around your neck and the toy binoculars over the shoulder.
7. Finishing touch: tuck the stuffed lion under one arm and practice your best explorer pose.
8. Optional pro finish: make a press pass on an index card (name plus STAFF PHOTOGRAPHER) and hang it from a lanyard or string.

Q: What is the cheapest way to make the binoculars?
A: Tape two empty paper towel rolls together and color them black with a marker. Thread a string through them as a neck strap.

Q: Do I need to buy a safari hat?
A: Any wide-brim hat from home works. A straw garden hat or a floppy sun hat reads as safari instantly with the khaki outfit.

### Safari / Zoo Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/safari-zoo-crew

Everyone picks an animal: closet clothes in matching colors plus an ear headband.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Solid-color clothes in animal colors, 1 set per person (own)
- Plastic headbands, 1 per person (buy: dollar store multi-pack)
- Felt sheets in brown, black, pink, tan, 1 pack (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Face paint in brown and black, 1 tube each (buy: costume aisle or craft store)
- Scissors and tape, 1 set (own)

Steps:
1. Assign roles BEFORE building. One guide per three animals keeps the ratio fun. Each person picks one animal and pulls matching solid-color clothes from the closet.
2. Safety: Cut the felt slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
3. Make each animal's ears from felt: cut two rounded ears and tape them to a plastic headband.
4. Safety: Use non-toxic kids face paint, and keep it away from the eyes.
5. Paint faces: use the face paint to add each animal's nose, whiskers, or spots.
6. Wear the colored outfit and put on the ear headband. Add one felt detail, like a felt tail taped to the back, to complete each animal.
7. Optional pro finish: the guide 'discovers' each animal with the binoculars throughout the night, announcing the species dramatically. The discovery bit is the group performance.

Q: How many animals per guide?
A: Two to four. One guide herding six animals is chaos; one guide with two animals is a duo. Three animals is the sweet spot.

Q: What animals are easiest?
A: Lion (ears plus painted nose), zebra (striped face paint), giraffe (ears plus spot paint). Pick animals with one iconic feature each.

### Salt & Pepper

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/salt-pepper

White and black outfits with shaker tops made from cardboard.

Build time, effort: 15 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- White shirt, pants, and hat for Salt, 1 set (own)
- Black shirt, pants, and hat for Pepper, 1 set (own)
- Cardboard for 2 shaker tops (make: from home)
- Gray paint or gray marker, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Black marker for the S and P, 1 (own)
- Tape or glue, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Salt dresses all in white, Pepper all in black.
2. Cut two shaker tops from cardboard: a short wide cylinder or dome each, big enough to sit on a hat.
3. Paint them gray and dot holes on top like a real shaker. Let dry.
4. Tape each top to a hat so it rides on your head.
5. Letter the caps BIG. Four-inch letters minimum, because the letter is the costume. Write a big S on Salt's shaker and a big P on Pepper's with the black marker.
6. Optional pro finish: carry actual salt and pepper shakers and offer to 'season' people's costumes. The seasoning bit is the party trick, use it liberally.

Q: How do you make the shaker tops?
A: Cut a short wide cylinder or dome from cardboard that fits over a hat, tape it shut, paint it gray, and dot holes on top like a real shaker.

Q: Who is salt and who is pepper?
A: Taller person is pepper (the bigger shaker energy), or whoever wants to be. There is no wrong answer.

### Friendly Scarecrow

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/scarecrow

Plaid shirt, straw poking out, and a stitched smile.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Plaid flannel shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Jeans with patches, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Straw, raffia, or yellow yarn, 1 bag (buy: craft store)
- Old hat, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Face paint in black and red, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Rope or twine, 1 coil (buy: hardware store)
- Safety pins, 4 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Stuff straw into the shirt cuffs, collar, and pant legs so it pokes out.
2. Tie straw bundles around the wrists and ankles with twine.
3. Paint a stitched smile and triangle nose on the face.
4. Wear the plaid shirt with patched jeans and the old hat.

6. Optional pro finish: stand perfectly still when trick-or-treaters approach, then wave. The stillness is the scare.

Q: How do you keep the straw from falling out?

Two graham-cracker tunics with a marshmallow and chocolate candy square between you.

### Ice Kingdom Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/snow-sisters

The ice queen, the snow princess, the talking snowman, the reindeer: pick your role.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Icy-blue dress or blue dress plus silver glitter glue, 1 set (buy glitter glue: craft store)
- Pink or lavender dress, 1 (own)
- White shirt, white pants, 3 large black felt circles (buy felt: craft store)
- Brown clothes, 2 brown pipe cleaners, 1 red pom-pom (buy: craft store)
- Silver headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Tape and scissors, 1 set (own)

Steps:
1. Assign roles, then buy the silver glitter glue, black felt circles, brown pipe cleaners, red pom-pom, and silver headband.
2. Pull the dresses and the white and brown clothes from closets. The snow princess just wears her dress, no crafting needed.
3. Test the glitter pattern on paper first. Glued glitter cannot be repositioned.
4. Spread the silver glitter glue in thin lines along the neckline and sleeves, and let it dry FLAT for one hour. Glue dried on a hanger drips.
5. Safety: Cut slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
6. Snowman: tape the 3 black felt circles down the front of the white shirt as coal buttons.
7. Reindeer: twist the 2 brown pipe cleaners into antler shapes and tape them to the silver headband. Tape the red pom-pom over the nose as a glowing nose.
8. Wear each outfit with its accessories. The ice queen adds the silver headband as a tiara.
9. Optional pro finish: the ice queen wears the silver headband as a tiara in every photo. The tiara is what separates the ice queen from a girl in a blue dress.

Q: How do you keep the glitter glue from cracking?
A: Thin lines, dried flat, fully cured. Thick blobs crack when the fabric moves. One thin coat beats two thick ones.

Q: What if the felt circles peel off the snowman?
A: Tape them from inside the shirt, not outside. Inside tape holds through a whole night of hugs; outside tape peels by hour two.

### Soccer Squad

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/soccer-squad

Jerseys for the players, black for the ref, one red card.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Matching jerseys or same-color t-shirts, 1 per player (own: from closet, or buy a multi-pack at a sports store)
- Black shirt and black shorts for the referee, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Soccer ball, 1 any size (buy: sports store, or borrow from home)
- Red cardstock rectangle, 3x4 inches, 1 (own: cut from a folder or colored paper)
- Black marker, 1 (own: from home)
- White athletic tape, 1 roll (buy: sports store or pharmacy)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Assign roles: most of the family are players, one person is the referee.
2. Players: wear matching jerseys or same-color shirts. Wrap a strip of white athletic tape around one upper arm as a captain's armband. Referee: wear all black.
3. Safety: Cut the cardstock slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Cut the red cardstock rectangle a little larger than 3x4 inches first, then trim to size after holding it up to check it reads at arm's length.
5. Make the red card: cut the rectangle from the folder or colored paper. Draw a thick black border around it with the black marker so it reads as a card at a glance.
6. Players carry or dribble the soccer ball. The referee practices holding the red card high in the air.
7. Optional pro finish: give the referee a coin for the coin toss and a small notebook as the official match log.

Q: What if we do not own matching jerseys?
A: Same-color t-shirts from the closet work fine. A multi-pack of plain tees from a sports store is the cheap fix for a big squad.

Q: How does the captain's armband stay on?
A: Wrap one strip of white athletic tape around one upper arm over the sleeve and press the ends together. It holds for the night and peels off after.

### Space Crewmate

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/space-crewmate

Colored sweatsuit plus a cardboard backpack.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Plain sweatsuit in one solid color, red recommended, 1 set (buy: a set at a discount store, or own: from closet)
- Cardboard, 1 sheet about 12x16 inches (own: from a box flap)
- Aluminum foil, about 2 feet (own: from the kitchen)
- Backpack straps, 2, or 2 long shoelaces (own: from home)
- Markers, 3 to 4 colors (own: from home)
- Tape, 1 roll (own: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Dress in the solid-color sweatsuit.
2. If you have more than one person, give each a different color.
3. Wrap the cardboard in aluminum foil for the backpack. Draw vents, dials, and one big red button with the markers. Tape the two backpack straps to the back of the cardboard.

### Spaghetti & Meatball

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/spaghetti-meatball

White shirt with yarn spaghetti glued on, brown pom-pom meatballs.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- White t-shirt or sweatshirt, 1 (own: from closet)
- Yellow or cream yarn, 1 skein (buy: craft store)
- Brown pom-poms, 2 inch, 3 to 4 (buy: craft store)
- Fabric glue or hot glue gun, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Lay the white shirt flat.
2. Lay out the yarn strands on the shirt first WITHOUT glue to check the wavy rows cover the shirt the way you want.
3. Then cut the yarn into 12-inch strands and glue them across the shirt in wavy rows to look like spaghetti, since glued strands cannot be repositioned.
4. Glue 3-4 brown pom-poms on top as meatballs.
5. Let dry completely before wearing.
6. Optional pro finish: glue a few small white pom-poms among the yarn as grated parmesan, and add a red felt meatball-sauce splatter on one sleeve.

Q: Can you wash the shirt after?
A: No. The glued yarn does not survive the washing machine. Treat it as a single-use costume shirt, so use a thrifted one you do not mind retiring.

Q: How long does the glue need to dry?
A: Let it dry completely before wearing, at least 1 hour for fabric glue. Lay it flat while drying so the yarn rows do not slide.

### Eight-Legged Spider

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/spider

Black sweats with stuffed sock legs attached at the sides.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 1 hr drying / Medium

Materials:
- Black sweatshirt and black sweatpants, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Black socks, 8 (4 pairs, own: from the sock drawer)
- Newspaper or tissue paper, 3 to 4 sheets, for stuffing (own: from home)
- Thin black rope or black yarn, 4 feet (buy: craft store)
- Black fabric glue, 1 bottle, or a needle and black thread (buy: craft store)
- Large googly eyes, 2 (buy: craft store; drawn paper circles work too)
- White face paint, 1 tube (buy: craft store or costume aisle)

Steps:
1. Stuff each of the 8 socks about half full with crumpled newspaper or tissue. Leave the top half empty so each leg can bend.
2. Pin the stuffed socks in place on the sweatshirt first and check the spacing in a mirror before committing.
3. Then use the black fabric glue or a few stitches to attach 4 stuffed socks down each side of the sweatshirt, spaced so they stick out like legs, since glued legs cannot be moved.
4. Poke the black yarn through the middle of each stuffed sock and tie it for a knee bend.
5. Glue one googly eye on each shoulder of the sweatshirt. Dress in the black sweatshirt and black sweatpants, then put on the leg-covered sweatshirt.
6. Safety: Use non-toxic face paint, and keep the googly eyes on the shoulders, not near the face.
7. Dot the white face paint around the eyes as spider markings.
8. Optional pro finish: run one long strand of black yarn across the back of the sweatshirt like a web anchor line, and add small white face-paint dots down the outside of each leg.

Q: How do you keep the sock legs from drooping?
A: Stuff each sock only half full and leave the top half empty so the leg can bend. Poke the black yarn through the middle of each sock and tie it for a knee bend, which holds the shape up.

Q: Can the sweatshirt be washed after?
A: Spot clean only. The glued-on legs will not survive a wash, so use a sweatshirt you are fine retiring to the costume bin.

### Sun and Moon

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/sun-moon

One in yellow with cardboard rays, one in navy with paper stars and a crescent.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Yellow shirt and pants for the Sun, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Navy or black shirt and pants for the Moon, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Yellow cardstock, 2 sheets (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Silver star stickers, 1 sheet (buy: craft store; cut paper stars work too)
- White and yellow paper, 1 sheet each, for the crescent (own: from home)
- Tape, 1 roll, and scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. One person dresses head to toe in yellow, the other in navy or black.
2. Buy the yellow cardstock and the silver star stickers.
3. Safety: Cut the cardstock slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Cut one ray first and tape it to the neckline to test the length before cutting the other nine, since cardstock cannot be lengthened.
5. Make the sun rays: cut 10 long triangles from the yellow cardstock, then tape them around the neckline and sleeves of the yellow shirt so they point outward.
6. Cut a large crescent from the white paper and tape it to the chest of the navy shirt. Scatter the silver star stickers across the shirt and arms.
7. Finishing touch: the Sun spreads arms wide to show the rays while the Moon holds one hand near the crescent.
8. Optional pro finish: glue the rays in pairs back to back so they are stiff and yellow on both sides, and edge the crescent with silver marker.

Q: How do you keep the sun rays from flopping over?
A: Tape each ray in pairs back to back so the cardstock is double thick, and tape a full inch of the ray base flat to the shirt. Short wide triangles flop less than long skinny ones.

Q: Will the tape damage the shirts?
A: Masking tape or painter's tape peels off clean. Packing tape holds better but can pull at fabric, so stick with the gentler tapes on clothes you want to keep.

---

### Superhero Family

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/superhero-family

Red sweatsuits, black eye masks, felt logo. The whole family goes super.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Matching red sweatsuits, 1 per person (buy: a set at a discount store, or own: from closet)
- Black felt, 1 pack (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Yellow felt, 1 sheet (buy: craft store)
- Plain headbands, 1 per person (buy: dollar store multi-pack)
- Safety pins, 6 to 8, or tape, 1 roll (own: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Have everyone dress in the red sweatsuits.
2. Safety: Cut the eye holes wide enough so everyone can see clearly.
3. Trace the eye holes by holding the felt strip up to each face and marking the pupil spots.
4. Cut the eye holes SMALLER than the marks first and widen as needed, since cut felt cannot be uncut.
5. Make the eye masks: cut a mask strip from the black felt for each person with two eye holes. Attach it to the headband with the safety pins or tape.
6. Make the logos: cut one big first-initial letter per person from the yellow felt. Use the safety pins or tape to attach it to the chest of each sweatsuit.
7. Everyone wears the mask headband with the letter on the chest. Each person strikes their own hero pose for the group photo.
8. Optional pro finish: cut a small yellow felt lightning bolt and pin one to each sleeve, so the emblem repeats beyond the chest.

Q: How do the masks stay on kids?
A: Attach the felt mask to a headband, not to the skin. The headband does the holding, so the mask never slips into the eyes.

Q: Are safety pins safe on kids' costumes?
A: Pin from the outside of the fabric so pin backs face the clothes, never the skin. For toddlers, use tape instead of pins everywhere.

### Sushi Roll

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/sushi-roll

A white-sheet wrap with felt salmon and pom-pom wasabi. Chopsticks optional.

Build time, effort: 40 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- White bedsheet or large white t-shirt to wear, 1 (own: from closet)
- Dark green felt, 1 large sheet (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Pink or orange felt, 1 large sheet (buy: craft store)
- White pom-poms, 4 large, plus 1 green pom-pom (buy: craft store; cotton balls work too)
- Toy chopsticks, 1 pair, or 2 wooden sticks (buy: toy store or craft store; pencils work too)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Dress in the white bedsheet or large white t-shirt.
2. Safety: Cut the felt slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
3. Wrap the felt band around the waist first and mark where it overlaps before cutting, since the band must meet around the body.
4. Make the wrap: cut the dark green felt sheet into a wide band that goes around your waist. Glue or pin it there as the seaweed wrap.
5. Make the toppings: cut the pink felt sheet into long strips and glue them across the white shirt as salmon.
6. Glue the white pom-poms near the shoulder as rice balls and the green pom-pom as wasabi.
7. Finishing touch: carry the toy chopsticks in one hand like you are about to pick up a bite.
8. Optional pro finish: tie a thin red ribbon belt over the seaweed wrap like the band on a real sushi roll, and glue sesame dots (tiny white paper circles) on the salmon strips.

Q: How do you wear a bedsheet without it falling off?
A: Wear a white t-shirt under it and safety-pin the sheet at both shoulders like a toga. Belt it with the seaweed wrap so it cannot unwrap.

Q: Will the waistband be comfortable all night?
A: Keep the band snug but loose enough to sit down in. Pinning instead of gluing lets you adjust it, and felt has a little give.

### Sushi & Soy Sauce

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/sushi-soy

White rice tunic with orange fish sash for one, dark soy bottle for the other.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- White t-shirt or tunic, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Dark brown or black t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Orange craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Black craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Cardboard for the soy bottle, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Dark brown acrylic paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Red paper for the bottle cap, 1 sheet (buy: dollar store)
- Ribbon for straps, about 2 yards (buy: craft store)
- Tape, 1 roll
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy the felt, paint, and ribbon. Pull a white and a dark t-shirt from the closet.
2. Sushi: cut an orange felt rectangle about the size of a paperback and glue it across the chest of the white t-shirt. This is the salmon.
3. Cut a black felt band 3 inches wide and glue it around the waist over the orange rectangle, like the seaweed holding the fish on.
4. Soy sauce: cut a tall bottle shape from the cardboard, about 2 feet tall, with a narrow neck.
5. Paint the bottle dark brown and let it dry flat. Fold red paper into a cap and tape it to the neck.
6. Tape ribbon loops to the top of the bottle and wear it like a sandwich board over the dark t-shirt.
7. Safety: Round all cardboard corners with the scissors so nobody gets poked in a crowd.
8. Optional pro finish: the sushi person leans toward the soy bottle in every photo. The dip is the pose.

Q: How do you keep the cardboard bottle from folding?
A: Use double-wall cardboard from a shipping box, not a cereal box, and keep the bottle under 2 feet tall.

Q: What if the paint is still tacky at party time?
A: Paint the bottle first and let it dry while you build the sushi. Dark paint needs a full hour on cardboard.

### Tall Hat Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tall-hat-crew

A striped stovepipe hat, a bow tie, and two wild blue-haired Things.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- Tall red-and-white striped stovepipe hat, 1 (buy: costume aisle, or make: poster board)
- Red bow tie, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: paper)
- Black shirt and pants for the cat, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Red jumpsuits or red shirts and pants for the Things, 2 sets (buy: 2 sets at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Blue wigs, 2 (buy: costume aisle)
- Iron-on letters or paper that says Thing 1 and Thing 2, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Iron, 1, and scissors, 1 pair (own: household)

Steps:
1. Cat: wear the black shirt and pants, the tall striped hat, and the red bow tie.
2. Position the paper letters on each chest and check the spelling and straightness in a mirror BEFORE ironing, since iron-on letters cannot be removed.
3. Things: wear the red jumpsuits with the blue wigs. Iron or tape Thing 1 and Thing 2 onto the chests.
4. The Things bounce and cause trouble; the cat looks worried. That is the whole photo.
5. Optional pro finish: add white gloves for the Things and a red ribbon tail on the cat, both cheap and both sell the characters.

Q: How do you make the tall hat from poster board?
A: Roll the poster board into a tall cone and tape the seam, then cut a wide circle with a hole for the brim and tape it to the base. Paint or tape on the red stripes.

Q: How does the tall hat stay on?
A: Thread an elastic chin string through the sides or anchor it with bobby pins through the hat into the hair. A snug inner band of folded paper helps too.

### Tennis Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tennis-duo

All-white outfits, headbands, toy rackets, and a tube of balls.

Build time, effort: 20 min / Easy

Materials:
- White t-shirts and white shorts or skirts, 1 set each (own: from closet)
- White sweatbands, 2, or strips of white fabric (buy: sports store)
- Toy tennis rackets, 2 (buy: toy store; cardboard rackets work too)
- Tennis balls, 1 tube of 3 (buy: sports store)
- White socks and sneakers, 1 pair each (own: from closet)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Pull the white outfits and sneakers from the closet.
2. Dress head to toe in white and tie the sweatband across the forehead.
3. Safety: Cut the fabric slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Measure the strip around the head with a finger's width of slack before cutting, then cut the 2-inch strip of white fabric.
5. To make a sweatband: tie it around the head with a knot at the back, snug enough to stay but loose enough to be comfortable.
6. Finishing touch: carry the toy tennis rackets and tuck the tube of balls under one arm for the courtside pose.
7. Optional pro finish: add a white wristband on the racket arm and tuck one spare ball into the waistband for the between-points look.

Q: How do you make a cardboard tennis racket?
A: Cut an oval with a handle from cardboard, cut out the middle, and weave string or yarn across the opening for the strings. Tape the handle for a grip.

Q: How do you keep the fabric sweatband from slipping?
A: Tie it with a knot at the back rather than relying on stretch. A knot you can retie stays put through the whole night.

### Block Party Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tetris-duo

Two interlocking tetromino shapes built from painted cardboard boxes, worn like sandwich boards.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 2 hrs drying / Easy

Materials:
- Two large cardboard boxes, flattened (make: from shipping boxes)
- Acrylic paint in two bright colors, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Wide ribbon or webbing for shoulder straps, about 4 yards (buy: craft store)
- Painter's tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors or a box cutter, 1
- Ruler or yardstick, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Mark a grid of 12-inch squares on the cardboard with the ruler.
2. Each block shape is 4 squares: cut an L shape for one person and a T or square shape for the other. Cut the squares oversized first and trim after a fitting.
3. Paint each shape its color and let dry fully, flat, for at least 2 hours.
4. Tape ribbon loops to the top of each shape for shoulder straps. Test the hang before the party: each shape should sit at chest height.
5. Safety: Cut on a protected surface with the blade pointed away from fingers, and round the cardboard corners so nobody gets poked in a crowd.
6. Each person wears one shape like a sandwich board, front and back panels tied with the ribbon straps.
7. Optional pro finish: stand so the two shapes interlock for photos, and let strangers name your pieces. The click-together pose is the whole costume.

Q: What are the easiest block shapes to build?
A: The 2 by 2 square and the L shape: both are rectangles with one extra cut, no fiddly notches. Paint them different colors so they read as two pieces.

Q: How do you keep the cardboard from flopping?
A: Use double-wall cardboard from a shipping box, not a cereal box, and keep each piece to 4 squares. Bigger pieces fold at the seams.

### The Olympians

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/the-olympians

Bedsheet togas, gold rope belts, laurel crowns. Pick your god: lightning bolt, owl, or trident.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 10 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- White bedsheets or large white fabric, 1 per person (own: raid the linen closet)
- Gold rope or gold cord, 2 yards per person (buy: craft store)
- Gold paper or gold craft leaves for laurel crowns, 1 pack (buy: craft store; gold paper works too)
- Gold face paint or gold eyeliner, 1 (buy: drugstore)
- Cardboard for the props, 3 pieces: lightning bolt, trident, owl (own: from boxes)
- Gold markers or gold paint pen, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Safety pins, 6 to 8; scissors, 1 pair; tape, 1 roll (own: household)

Steps:
1. Make the togas: wrap one sheet around each person over a plain t-shirt and shorts, pinning at the shoulder with a safety pin. Belt it with the gold rope.
2. Safety: Pin from the outside of the fabric so pin backs face the clothes, never the skin. Keep the toga above the ankles so nobody trips.
3. Size the paper strip around each head and overlap it by an inch before taping, since tape cannot be repositioned cleanly.
4. Make the laurel crowns: cut leaf shapes from the gold paper and tape them along a paper strip sized to each head.
5. Make the god props: cut a lightning bolt, a trident, and an owl from the cardboard. Color them gold with the markers.
6. Paint one gold detail on each face: a lightning streak, an owl feather, or a wave. Each god picks a power pose for the group photo.
7. Optional pro finish: wrap gold cord around each wrist as a cuff and tie gold cord laces up the calves over the shoes for the sandal look.

Q: How do you keep the toga from falling off?
A: Wear a plain t-shirt and shorts under it, pin the sheet at the shoulder, and belt it with the gold rope at the natural waist. The belt does most of the holding.

Q: Is a floor-length sheet a tripping hazard?
A: Keep the toga hem above the ankles and pin the extra fabric up. Test walking and stairs before leaving the house.

### The Tin Hero

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tin-hero

Red and gold plus a glowing chest circle: the suit does the talking.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Red sweatsuit, 1 (buy: at a discount store, or own: from closet)
- Gold duct tape, 1 roll (buy: dollar store or hardware store)
- Battery tea light, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Cardboard, 1 piece (own)
- Tape, 1 roll (own)
- Safety pin, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Dress in the red sweatsuit.
2. Stripe the sweatsuit with the gold duct tape: strips across the chest, arms, and legs.
3. Draw the reactor circle on the cardboard BEFORE cutting, and measure it against the chest first. Cover it in gold tape, then tape the tea light behind its center.
4. Safety: Pin from inside the sweatsuit, so the pin back faces the fabric and never the skin.
5. Pin the glowing circle to the chest of the sweatsuit.
6. Walk like the suit does the talking.
7. Optional pro finish: pin the reactor slightly off-center, like battle damage. Perfectly centered reads as costume; off-center reads as character.

Q: How does the chest reactor glow?
A: A battery tea light taped behind a cardboard circle covered in gold tape. The tape diffuses the light so it glows instead of showing a bulb.

Q: Will the duct tape peel off the sweatsuit?
A: Press each strip down hard and smooth out air bubbles. Fresh duct tape holds all night; old tape from the junk drawer peels by dinner.

### Tiny Firefighter

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tiny-firefighter

Red sweats, a plastic helmet, and a toy hose.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Red sweatsuit, 1 (buy: at a discount store, or own: from closet)
- Toy firefighter helmet, 1 (buy: toy store)
- Toy fire hose or coiled garden hose, 1 (buy: toy store, or borrow a real coil of rope from home)
- Yellow reflective tape, 1 roll (buy: hardware store)
- Black marker, 1 (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Make the turnout stripes: wrap two horizontal bands of the yellow reflective tape around each sleeve and each leg. Press the tape firmly so it sticks.
2. Safety: Keep the toy firefighter helmet snug so it does not slide over the eyes.
3. Put the toy firefighter helmet on and carry the toy fire hose coiled over one shoulder.
4. Finishing touch: the kid holds the hose nozzle out front for the hero photo.
5. Optional pro finish: wrap one band of reflective tape around the toy helmet too, so the whole uniform matches.

Q: Will the reflective tape come off the sweatsuit after?
A: It peels off, but it can leave sticky residue on some fabrics. Test a hidden spot first, and use a thrifted sweatsuit if you want zero risk.

Q: What if the toy helmet is too big and slides over the eyes?
A: Stuff folded paper towel inside the helmet until it sits snug. Keep it snug enough that it never slides over the eyes.

### Tiny Snail

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tiny-snail

Neutral clothes plus a lightweight spiral shell from cardboard worn like a backpack.

Build time, effort: 30 min / Easy

Materials:
- Neutral beige or tan clothes, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Large cardboard sheet or 1 flattened box (own: from home)
- Brown and tan markers or crayons, 1 set (own: from home)
- Backpack straps, 2, or 2 long ribbons (own: from home)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Black pom-poms, 2 (buy: craft store; cotton balls work too)
- Tape, 1 roll (own: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Dress the kid in the beige or tan clothes.
2. Buy the headband and black pom-poms.
3. Safety: Cut the cardboard slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
4. Draw the oval on the cardboard first and hold it against the kid's back to check the size before cutting, since a too-small shell cannot be fixed.
5. Make the shell: cut the cardboard into a large oval. Draw a spiral from the center outward with the brown marker. Tape the two backpack straps to the back so it wears like a backpack.
6. Make the eyestalks: tape two short cardboard strips to the headband so they point up. Tape a black pom-pom to the top of each strip.
7. Wear the shell backpack and the headband with the pom-pom eyestalks. Keep the shell light and the straps snug so it rides comfortably.
8. Optional pro finish: edge the shell oval with a tan marker border and add a second smaller spiral inside the first for a realistic shell pattern.

Q: How do you keep the shell light enough for a small kid?
A: Use single-ply cardboard from a cereal-style box rather than a heavy shipping box, and keep the oval modest. Tape, don't glue, so it stays light.

Q: How do you keep the eyestalks standing up?
A: Use short cardboard strips, about 4 inches, and small pom-poms. Tall strips with big pom-poms flop over every time.
