### Tooth and Tooth Fairy

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/tooth-fairy

One all-white with a cardboard tooth outline; the other adds wings and an envelope of tooth money.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 30 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- Tooth: all-white outfit, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Tooth fairy: white dress or white shirt with a white skirt, 1 (own: from closet)
- White cardstock, 1 large sheet (buy: craft store)
- White felt wings, 1 pair, or 1 wire coat hanger with white pantyhose (buy: craft store, or make: from home)
- Small envelope and play money or a coin, 1 (own: from home)
- Glitter glue, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- Stick and aluminum foil for the wand, 1 (own: from home)
- Tape, 1 roll, and scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Pull the white clothes from the closet.
2. Draw the tooth outline lightly in pencil first and hold it against the chest to check the size before cutting.
3. Make the tooth: cut a large tooth shape with two roots from the white cardstock. Edge it with the glitter glue and let it dry. Tape it to the chest of the white outfit.
4. Safety: Tape down any sharp wire ends from the wire coat hanger, and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
5. Make the wings: stretch the white pantyhose over a reshaped wire coat hanger to form two wing loops.
6. Tape the hanger ends to a piece of cardboard worn at the back. Tuck the envelope with play money into a pocket or waistband.
7. Tooth fairy: wear the white dress and strap on the wings. Carry the wand made from the stick with an aluminum foil star taped on top.
8. Optional pro finish: tuck a tiny card into the envelope that says the tooth exchange rate (one tooth equals one wish) for the full fairy bureaucracy joke.

Q: How do two people split the tooth and the fairy?
A: One person wears the all-white outfit with the big tooth on the chest, the other wears the white dress with the wings and carries the wand and envelope. Both read clearly side by side.

Q: Is the wire hanger safe for wings?
A: Yes if you tape down every sharp wire end and keep the taped ends at the back on the cardboard. For small kids, use felt wings with no wire at all.

### Toy Box Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/toy-box-crew

A cowboy sheriff, a space ranger, and the rest of the toy box: pick your favorite.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Cowboy hat, 1, and cow-print vest, 1, for the sheriff (buy: costume aisle or thrift store)
- White shirt and pants, 1 set, with purple felt accents for the space ranger (own: from closet)
- Cardboard wings and 1 clear plastic dome for the space ranger helmet (own: from craft supplies)
- Brown boots or boot covers, 1 pair, for the sheriff (own: from closet)
- Yellow shirt, 1, with a hand-drawn star badge for extra toy-box friends (own: from closet)
- Toy pull-string name tags, 1 per person (own: index cards)
- Marker, 1; scissors, 1 pair; glue, 1 bottle; tape, 1 roll (own: household)

Steps:
1. Sheriff: wear the cowboy hat, cow-print vest, and brown boots. Draw a star badge on the yellow shirt with a marker.
2. Lay the felt fins and buttons on the white shirt first and check the placement in a mirror before gluing, since glued felt cannot be moved.

Q: How do the pull-string name tags work?

### Under the Sea

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/under-the-sea

Jellyfish from an umbrella with ribbon tentacles, crab from red clothes and claw mittens, plus fish, seaweed, and waves.

Build time, effort: 40 min / Easy

Materials:
- Jellyfish: 1 clear umbrella (buy: dollar store)
- Jellyfish: pastel ribbons, 1 spool (buy: craft store; crepe paper strips work too)
- Crab: red shirt and pants, 1 set, plus red mittens or red socks, 1 pair, for hands (own: from closet)
- Fish: silver or blue clothes, 1 set, and 1 large cardboard fish cutout (own: from home)
- Seaweed: green clothes, 1 set, and long green streamers, 1 pack (buy: party store)
- Waves: blue sheet or blue blanket, 1 (own: from home)
- Tape, 1 roll, and scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Assign one sea creature per person. Buy the clear umbrella, pastel ribbons, and green streamers. Pull the colored clothes from closets.
2. Safety: Cut the ribbons slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors. Hold the clear umbrella high and keep the tentacle ribbons clear of faces.
3. Cut one ribbon first and tape it to the umbrella edge to test the drape before cutting the rest.
4. Jellyfish: cut the pastel ribbons into 3-foot lengths. Tape them to the edge of the clear umbrella so they dangle like tentacles. Hold the clear umbrella overhead.
5. Crab: dress in red and slide the red mittens or red socks onto the hands.
6. Hold both hands up with fingers pinched like claws. Fish: tape the cardboard fish cutout to the chest over the silver clothes.
7. Seaweed: tape the green streamers to the shoulders and arms so they wave when the arms move. Everyone together can hold the blue sheet behind the group as a wave backdrop for the photo.
8. Optional pro finish: tape small silver star stickers to the ribbons as bubbles, and give the fish a paper gill slit detail with marker.

Q: Is the umbrella safe in a crowd?
A: Hold the clear umbrella high and keep the tentacle ribbons clear of faces. In tight crowds, carry it closed until there is room to open it.

Q: What if it actually rains?
A: The jellyfish wins: the umbrella is real and functional. The ribbons may get soggy, so use crepe paper only if the forecast is dry.

### Classic Vampire

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/vampire

Black cape, fangs, slicked hair.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Black cape or black bedsheet, 1 (buy cape: costume aisle; or make: from a black sheet from home)
- Black shirt and pants, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Plastic vampire fangs, 1 pair (buy: costume aisle or dollar store)
- Hair gel or pomade, 1 (own: from home)
- Red lipstick or red face paint, 1 (buy: pharmacy or costume aisle)
- White face powder or pale face paint, 1 (buy: costume aisle)

Steps:
1. Dress in the black shirt and pants.
2. Make the hair: work the hair gel through the hair with your fingers. Press it straight back until it sits flat and slick.
3. Safety: Use non-toxic costume makeup, and skip the vampire fangs for small kids who might choke on them.
4. Make the face: dust the pale face paint over the face and neck. Dab a thin line of red lipstick at each corner of the mouth like drips of blood.
5. Wear the black cape over the shoulders and pop the vampire fangs in last before photos.
6. Optional pro finish: paint the nails black and pop the cape collar up high, since the collar silhouette is what reads as vampire from across the room.
7. Safety: Add reflective tape or a glow stick and carry a flashlight for visibility at night.

Q: Are the plastic fangs safe for small kids?
A: Skip the fangs for small kids who might choke on them. Draw two white fang triangles on the lower lip with face paint instead.

Q: How do you get the pale face without buying special makeup?
A: White face powder from the costume aisle is cheapest. Whatever you use, patch-test it first on sensitive skin and wash it off the same night.

### Walking Taco

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/walking-taco

Tan vest painted like a taco shell with felt toppings.

Build time, effort: 45 min + 30 min drying / Medium

Materials:
- Tan vest or tan t-shirt, 1 (own: from closet)
- Brown, red, green, and yellow felt sheets, 1 pack (buy: craft store; construction paper works too)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Dress the kid in the tan vest or tan t-shirt.
2. Safety: Cut the felt slowly and keep fingers clear of the scissors.
3. Pin or lay the brown felt strips on the vest first and check the fold placement in a mirror before gluing, since glued felt cannot be repositioned.
4. Glue two curved strips of brown felt down the front of the tan vest to form the shell fold.
5. Make the toppings: cut wavy strips of green felt for lettuce and red circles for tomatoes. Cut yellow rectangles for cheese and brown blobs for beef.
6. Glue them in a row across the chest and shoulders so they spill out like a taco filling.
7. Make the headband garnish: glue one green felt strip and one red felt circle to the headband. Wear it with the vest as a lettuce and tomato topper.
8. Optional pro finish: glue a fringe of thin yellow felt strips along the bottom edge of the vest so cheese spills out all around.

Q: Can you wash the vest after Halloween?
A: No. The glued felt does not survive the washing machine. Spot clean only, and use a vest you are fine keeping as a costume.

Q: Felt or construction paper for the toppings?
A: Felt survives the whole night; construction paper tears and wilts with any moisture. Felt is worth it for a kid who will be running around.

### Wayfinder Princess

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/wayfinder-princess

A printed sailcloth top, grass skirt, and a cardboard hook.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 1 hr drying / Easy

Materials:
- Tan or brown tank top, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Crepe paper or raffia for the skirt, 2 rolls (buy: craft store)
- Cardboard for the hook, 1 sheet (make: from a shipping box)
- Brown paint, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Shell necklace, 1 (buy: dollar store, or make: from pasta shells and string)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Cut the crepe paper into long strips and tie them around an elastic waistband for the skirt.
2. Paint a spiral design on the tank top with the brown paint.
3. Cut the hook shape from cardboard and paint it brown.
4. Wear the shell necklace and carry the cardboard hook.
5. Safety: Keep the hook cardboard and light, never swung near faces, and round all edges.
6. Optional pro finish: practice one confident stance with the hook raised. The stance is the character.

Q: How do you keep the paper skirt from tearing?
A: Tie each strip separately rather than gluing a sheet. Separate strips move and survive sitting.

Q: What if the hook is too big to carry?
A: Scale it to forearm length. A smaller hook carried confidently beats a big one left at home.

---

### Web Hero Duo

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/web-hero-duo

Red-blue sweatsuit plus web mask; partner gets the black jacket and attitude.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Hero: red and blue sweatsuit, or red shirt with blue pants, 1 set (buy: a set at a discount store, or own: from closet)
- Partner: black jacket and black pants, 1 set (own: from closet)
- Black face paint or black eye mask, 1 (buy: costume aisle)
- White face paint or white stickers, 1 (buy: craft store)
- Red web gloves or red socks for hands, 1 pair (own: from closet)
- Tape, 1 roll (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Pull the red and blue outfit and the black jacket and black pants from closets.
2. Safety: Use non-toxic face paint, and keep paint out of the eyes.
3. Test the white web pattern on a paper towel first to check the paint flow, since painted lines cannot be undone on fabric.
4. Hero: paint a black eye mask with the black face paint across the eyes.
5. Add white web lines over the red shirt using the white face paint.
6. Or tear thin strips of tape in a web pattern over the shirt. Pull the red socks onto the hands as web gloves.
7. Partner: wear the black jacket and black pants and slick the hair back. Strike the brooding pose. No crafting needed beyond the outfit.
8. Finishing touch: the hero throws one arm out in a web-shooting pose while the partner crosses their arms behind them.
9. Optional pro finish: run the white tape web pattern across the back of the shirt too, so the costume reads from behind in photos.

Q: Will the white paint ruin the red shirt?
A: Yes, face paint stains fabric. If you want the shirt wearable after, use white stickers or thin tape strips in a web pattern instead of paint.

Q: What is safer around the eyes, paint or a mask?
A: A black eye mask avoids paint near the eyes entirely. If you paint, keep all paint above the cheekbones and below the brow, never on the lids.

### Web Hero Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/web-slinger-crew

Red, black, and pink hoodies plus masks. Pick your spider.

Build time, effort: 30 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Hoodies in red, black, and pink, 1 per person (buy: at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Black fabric paint or black face paint, 1 tube (buy: craft store)
- White stickers or white electrical tape, 1 roll (buy: hardware store)
- Sunglasses or swim goggles, 1 per person (buy: dollar store multi-pack)
- Tape, 1 roll (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Assign each person a hoodie color.
2. Buy the black fabric paint or black face paint, white stickers or white electrical tape, and the multi-pack of sunglasses.
3. Draw the eye-lens shape on paper first and hold it against the sunglasses to check the size before painting, since paint on lenses cannot be removed cleanly.
4. Stick white stickers or white electrical tape in a web pattern across the front of each pair of sunglasses.
5. Draw two black eye lenses on top with the black fabric paint or black face paint. Let them dry flat for 30 minutes.
6. Make the chest webs: stick short white tape strips in a web grid across the chest of each hoodie.
7. Wear the hoodie with the hood up and put on the web-patterned sunglasses. Each person picks their own web-shooting pose for the group shot.
8. Optional pro finish: run short white tape strips down the outside of each sleeve as web lines, so the arms match the chest.

Q: Sunglasses or swim goggles for the eye lenses?
A: Swim goggles stay on better, especially for kids running around. Sunglasses work for photos but slide off during the night.

Q: Will the electrical tape come off the hoodie after?
A: White electrical tape peels off clean from most hoodie fabrics. Test a hidden spot first on anything delicate.

### Web Hero

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/web-slinger-kid

Red sweatsuit, tape web lines, big white eye lenses.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Red sweatsuit or red shirt and pants, 1 set (buy: at a clothing store, or own: from closet)
- Blue craft felt for sleeve and boot accents, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store, blue paper works too)
- Black electrical tape for web lines, 1 roll (buy: hardware store)
- White paper or cardstock for eye lenses, 1 sheet (make: cut from paper)
- Plain headband, 1 (buy: dollar store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Lay the red sweatsuit flat and plan the web lines first: one center line down the chest, then fan lines out to each side.
2. Stick short strips of black electrical tape across the chest in a web grid, pressing each strip flat so it survives the night.
3. Cut two large white eye lenses from the white paper with the scissors. Hold them against the face to check the size before attaching.
4. Safety: Tape the paper eyes to the plain headband, never tape paper to skin around the eyes. Skip the eyes for very young kids and draw web lines with face paint instead.
5. Cut blue felt rectangles and tape them around the sleeves and pant cuffs as hero accents.
6. Pull on the red sweatsuit, put on the eye headband, and strike the web-shooter pose: one hand up, fingers spread.
7. Optional pro finish: run short black tape strips down the outside of each sleeve as web lines, so the arms match the chest.

Q: Will the tape ruin the sweatsuit?
A: Black electrical tape peels off most sweatshirt fabric cleanly. Test a hidden spot first, and pull it off slowly after the night.

Q: My kid will not wear a headband. What then?
A: Skip the paper eyes and draw simple black web lines on the cheeks with non-toxic face paint. The red suit plus web lines reads as the hero on its own.

### Wine & Cheese

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/wine-cheese

Burgundy wine glass tunic for one, yellow cheese wedge with holes for the other.

Build time, effort: 25 min + 30 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Burgundy or maroon t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Yellow t-shirt, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- White craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Burgundy craft felt, 1 sheet 9x12 inches (buy: craft store)
- Fabric glue, 1 bottle (buy: craft store)
- Scissors, 1 pair

Steps:
1. Buy the felt and glue. Pull a burgundy and a yellow t-shirt from the closet.
2. Wine: cut a wine glass shape from the white felt, bowl, stem, and base in one piece, about a foot tall.
3. Cut a smaller burgundy felt shape for the wine inside the glass and glue it onto the white glass.
4. Glue the finished glass centered on the burgundy t-shirt.
5. Cheese: cut round holes from a yellow felt triangle and pin it over the yellow t-shirt. Swiss reads instantly.
6. Safety: If cutting holes in the shirt itself, keep them small and away from the seams so the shirt holds its shape.
7. Optional pro finish: raise your glasses together for every photo. The toast is the costume, so commit to it.

Q: How do you cut clean holes in the cheese?
A: Fold the felt and cut half-circles along the fold, then unfold for perfect circles. Small scissors beat big ones for the curves.

Q: What if we cannot find a burgundy shirt?
A: A dark red shirt works. The wine glass felt carries the costume either way.

### Witchy Sister Trio

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/witchy-sisters

Three color-coded witch dresses: green, purple, and orange.

Build time, effort: 35 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Dresses in green, purple, and orange, 3 (buy: thrift store)
- Black witch hats, 3 (buy: dollar store, or make: from cardboard and felt)
- Broomsticks, 3 (buy: dollar store, or make: from sticks and straw)
- Face paint in matching colors, 1 set (buy: craft store)
- Striped tights, 3 pairs (buy: dollar store)

Steps:
1. Each sister claims a color: green, purple, or orange, and builds around it.
2. Wear the colored dress with a black witch hat and striped tights.
3. Paint a matching beauty mark or stripe in your color.
4. Safety: Keep broomsticks pointed down in crowds, and test face paint on a wrist first.
5. Cackle in unison when anyone takes your photo. The unison cackle is the act.
6. Optional pro finish: the green sister stands in the middle. The middle placement matches the legend.

Q: How do you keep three thrifted dresses looking like a set?
A: Matching hats and tights unify any three dresses. The accessories do the grouping, not the dresses.

Q: Can two people do this instead of three?
A: Two works, but the trio is the iconic number. Recruit a third; the spell needs three.

### Classic Wizard

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/wizard

Tall black pointy hat, flowing plain black robe, tall straight wooden staff, gray beard optional.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Tall black pointy wizard hat, 1 (buy: costume aisle or craft store)
- Long plain black robe or graduation gown, 1 (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Tall straight wooden staff, about 5 feet (make: from a dowel or sturdy branch, or buy: craft store)
- Gray face paint or stick-on gray beard, 1 (buy: costume aisle, optional)
- Belt or rope sash, 1 (own)

Steps:
1. Size the hat to the head BEFORE decorating, a hat decorated then found too small is heartbreaking. Put on the robe.
2. Roll the paper into a tall wizard hat or use the store-bought one; confirm it sits without covering the eyes. Stick the star stickers on the robe and hat.
3. Safety: Keep the hat brim above the eyes so vision stays clear, and carry the staff upright. Never swing it at anyone.
4. Draw on a gray beard with the face paint, or stick on the fake beard.
5. Tie the belt or rope sash around the waist over the robe.
6. Put on the pointy hat last, tap the staff on the ground, and strike a pose.
7. Optional pro finish: tape a battery tea light to the wand tip. A wand that glows when you cast is the detail kids remember for years, the gasps are worth the tape.

Q: How tall should the wizard hat be?
A: About as tall as the head. Taller looks impressive but flops without internal support, roll a cone of cardstock inside for structure.

Q: What goes in the spell book?
A: Write silly spells on the pages in marker ('Spell for extra dessert: say please three times'). People WILL open it, make it funny.

### Yellow Henchmen Crew

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/yellow-henchmen

Yellow shirts, blue overalls, and swim goggles for the whole crew.

Build time, effort: 25 min / Easy

Materials:
- Yellow t-shirts, 1 per person (buy: at a thrift store, or own: from closet)
- Blue overalls or blue jeans, 1 per person (own, or buy: thrift store)
- Swim goggles, 1 per person (buy: dollar store)
- Black gloves, 1 pair per person (buy: dollar store)
- Black marker, 1 (own)
- Bananas, 1 bunch (buy: grocery store)

Steps:
1. Everyone wears yellow on top and blue on the bottom. That is the whole uniform.
2. Wear the swim goggles on the forehead and draw one big eye on paper to tape inside each lens.
3. Carry the bananas everywhere and offer them to strangers.
4. Safety: Wear the goggles on the forehead, not over the eyes, so vision stays clear while walking.
5. Learn one shared gibberish phrase and say it in unison. The unison is the comedy.
6. Optional pro finish: the tallest henchman stands in the middle for photos. The height lineup makes the crew.

Q: How many people do you need?
A: Two works, five is ideal. The joke scales with the headcount.

Q: What if someone has no overalls?
A: Blue jeans with suspenders read the same. The yellow shirt and goggles carry it.

### Zombie Coworker

URL: https://pickmycostume.com/c/zombie-coworker

Torn button-down, loosened tie, pale makeup, coffee mug.

Build time, effort: 20 min + 10 min drying / Easy

Materials:
- Old button-down shirt you can cut up, 1 (own: from closet)
- Old tie, 1 (own: from closet)
- Pale face paint or white face powder, 1 (buy: costume aisle)
- Dark eye makeup or black eyeshadow, 1 (buy: pharmacy)
- Coffee mug, 1 (own: from home)
- Scissors, 1 pair (own: from home)

Steps:
1. Pull the old button-down shirt, old tie, and coffee mug from home.
2. Safety: Cut away from your fingers, and keep the scissors away from small kids. Use non-toxic costume makeup.
3. Decide where every slit goes and mark the spots with chalk before cutting, since cut fabric cannot be put back.
4. Make the torn shirt: cut jagged slits along the hem of the old button-down shirt and one sleeve. Tie the old tie loosely and crookedly around the neck.
5. Make the face: cover the face with the pale face paint. Ring the eyes with the dark eye makeup. Smudge a little down one cheek like a long night at the office.
6. Wear the torn shirt with the loosened tie and carry the coffee mug everywhere, mumbling about the quarterly review.
7. Optional pro finish: add a lanyard with a blank ID badge worn backwards, the universal sign of someone who gave up at 3pm.

Q: What if I do not want to ruin a real work shirt?
A: Buy a thrift-store button-down and destroy that instead. It looks more authentically worn-out anyway.

Q: How do you get the zombie makeup off?
A: Wash it off the same night with soap and warm water. Pale face paint stains pillowcases, so wash before bed, not in the morning.
